name: Soltāro
effect: The show is named Soltāro - solitaire plus Balatro plus the Latin for sun. The title card is itself a card in the menu troupe wagon.
note: Keep one canonical spelling with the macron; the ASCII fallback Solatro is the project folder name only.

name: The Greatest Deck on Earth
effect: Alternate show billings the marquee cycles through - Cardaganza, Circustaire, Showitaire, Patience-mania. The marquee picks one per run as the tour's poster.
note: Free flavor variety; the Barnum habit of stuffing titles into a circus name is authentic and already in the references.

name: Void Symphony cue
effect: Reference track for the between-shows map theme - sparse, patient, no percussion until a node is entered.
note: Reference only, never shipped audio.

name: Neon Nightlife cue
effect: Reference track for the show itself - the midway at night, driving and warm.
note: Reference only. Pairs with the warm-foreground palette rule.

name: Balatro-with-solitaire pillar
effect: The founding compression - Balatro's joker economy on a solitaire board. The grid overhaul keeps it: poker hands are still the meld vocabulary, effects are still the engine.
note: Survives the grid pivot untouched; it is the reason poker hands stayed when the tableau went.

name: Zachtronics and Hempuli study
effect: Study set for solitaire variants that carry a rules twist rather than a card twist - the Zachtronics collection and Hempuli's solitaire mystery.
note: Both are rules-deck arguments: change one rule, get a new game. That is what the rule deck is for.

name: Deck-click drop-down
effect: Every click of the deck dropped a new row of cards into the board and spent a round.
note: SUPERSEDED by the grid - cards are placed by hand, nothing drops, and the Next button is gone.

name: Free-space score slot
effect: The old score slot doubled as free parking between deck clicks. Revived as a grid cell that a blind or rule card marks reserved - it holds one card out of scoring until released.
note: Revived by the grid, not carried: a reserved cell is a cell that scores nothing until the rule card frees it.

name: Entrance mulligan
effect: Click cards in the Entrance and press discard to throw them back; the Entrance refills from the deck in random slot order.
note: The discard-as-engine essay's core ask. Costs a limited resource so it is not free filtering.

name: Entrance reorder
effect: Drag cards within the Entrance to change which column each one starts nearest. Order is information, not power.
note: Cheap comfort that becomes strategy once effects care which Entrance slot a card sat in.

name: Balatro chassis
effect: Jokers, consumables, shops, blinds and vouchers are taken as proven shapes and reskinned rather than reinvented.
note: The explicit instruction not to redesign solved problems. Blinds are the newest import.

name: Starting decks
effect: Each starting deck sets the initial card list AND the rule cards the run begins with, so a deck is a ruleset as much as a card list.
note: The rule deck makes this nearly free - a deck is a different rules deck.

name: Face cards count ten
effect: An optional rank rule where every face card counts as 10 for any summing meld - cribbage fifteens, the 20-30 row objective, the 31 count.
note: Only matters once a summing meld exists; ships with The Fifteen and the rank-sum blinds.

name: Fifteens
effect: Any set of cards in one scored line summing to exactly 15 banks a flat bonus, once per distinct set.
note: Cribbage's engine. Explicitly demoted from a default rule to an ability by a later draft line.

name: Thirty-ones
effect: Any set of cards in one scored line summing to exactly 31 banks a larger flat bonus.
note: The blackjack-adjacent sibling of fifteens; rarer because 31 is harder to reach in five cards.

name: Pair meld
effect: Two cards of equal rank in a scored line. The floor of the poker table and the unit the pair-count blinds count.
note: Already implemented by the poker evaluator; listed so blind objectives have a name to cite.

name: Triple meld
effect: Three of a kind in a scored line.
note: Implemented.

name: Quad meld
effect: Four of a kind in a scored line - in a five-card line this leaves exactly one odd card.
note: Implemented. The mahjong hands reuse this shape across a whole grid.

name: Run meld
effect: A consecutive rank sequence of three to seven cards. Lengths above five only exist on a long row spanning grids.
note: The long-row rule is what makes runs longer than five reachable at all.

name: Magic deck
effect: Every suit is an element and lines score as spells - a completed line of matching elements fires a spell instead of a poker hand.
note: A rules-deck swap of the meld evaluator; the cleanest proof the rule deck earns its keep.

name: Survivor deck
effect: Suits become supplies - food, water, blade, shelter - and a line scores by how balanced its supply mix is, punishing flushes.
note: The anti-flush deck. Pairs with the no-flush blind objective.

name: Number cards then face cards
effect: The tour's first half is number-ranked nodes; face-ranked nodes only open once the numbers are cleared, and they are the bosses.
note: Deadman Wonderland's stage gate, and a clean way to make face cards mean something on the map.

name: Card-marked map nodes
effect: Every map location is a single card - its suit is the kind of encounter, its rank the difficulty.
note: Already how the worldgen graph wants to be labelled; the card IS the node data.

name: Minesweeper reveal map
effect: The whole tour starts face down. You may only enter a node adjacent to one already revealed; entering reveals its neighbours.
note: Fog of war the player clears by playing, not by buying vision.

name: Sevens are shops
effect: Every rank-7 node on the map is a trading hall, so the player can read the map's economy at a glance.
note: Rank-as-node-type; makes the map legible without inventing icons.

name: Rank probability rings
effect: The map generates as concentric rings of rank probability - higher ranks cluster toward the centre, so distance from the middle reads as danger.
note: Fits the worldgen graph bake and gives the route a shape to plan against.

name: Revealed cards act
effect: Any card whose face is visible runs its effects; a face-down card runs nothing until something reveals it.
note: The blind that starts a face-down card on the board depends on this rule existing.

name: Grab from anywhere
effect: A stack may be lifted from any cell; an illegal stack may only be returned where it came from or sent to the Entrance.
note: In the grid game placement is one-way by default, so this is an effect-granted verb rather than a rule.

name: Booking the next entrance
effect: Clicking a card on the map sends it to the top of the deck, so it is the first Entrance card of the next show.
note: Lets the map shape the opening hand - a planning tool rather than a power spike.

name: Cards are currency
effect: There is no gold. A card's price is paid in cards drawn at random from your deck to the value of the price.
note: The thinning pressure IS the economy. Keeps the deck honest without a separate cut-a-card service.

name: Gold card
effect: Heavy denomination card - always sinks to the bottom of the deck after a shuffle and is only useful at a shop.
note: Implemented as TypeHeavy plus a token. Dead weight in the Ring is the price of being money.

name: Frankenstein
effect: Cue - merge this card with the cards directly above and below it into one three-rank card that keeps every stamp; the merged card stays in its cell.
note: Height makes this readable at last: the merge is visibly three storeys collapsing into one.

name: Sliced Bread
effect: When this card scores, gain a point for every card between it and the nearest same-suit card further down its stack.
note: Reads perfectly on a vertical stack; on the old tableau it was invisible.

name: Double Trigger stamp
effect: This card's effects trigger twice.
note: Implemented as StampDoubleTrigger. The workhorse stamp.

name: Revealing stamp
effect: Triggers even while covered by cards above it in its stack.
note: Implemented as StampRevealing. Height stacking is exactly what makes it valuable now.

name: Deck trigger stamp
effect: This card's skill fires while it is still in the draw deck; the trigger animates above the deck slot so it is visible.
note: Global by definition - a card in the deck belongs to no grid.

name: Brass Check stamp
effect: On trigger, mint one Gold card onto the top of the deck.
note: The money-on-trigger seal with a circus name. Global because it writes to the deck.

name: Heavy type
effect: Sinks to the bottom of the deck on every shuffle.
note: Implemented as TypeHeavy.

name: Light type
effect: Rises to the top of the deck on every shuffle - the reliable-draw counterpart to Heavy.
note: Trivially the mirror of TypeHeavy and worth printing for that reason.

name: Elemental types
effect: Earth sits at the bottom, Air at the top, Water moves one position per shuffle, Fire burns itself out of the deck after a set number of shows.
note: Four deck-position behaviours from one visual family; Fire overlaps Glass deliberately.

name: Whole-board submission
effect: The entire board was evaluated once, when the player pressed submit.
note: SUPERSEDED - lines score the instant they complete, and End now only fires hooks.

name: Row-wide poker hands
effect: A five-wide board is exactly a poker hand wide, which is why rows score as poker and columns as runs.
note: The load-bearing coincidence the whole design rests on.

name: Legal stacks only
effect: A stack may only be lifted if it is internally legal; the rule lives on the topmost card's suit, not in the engine.
note: Implemented through the pip comparator. Height stacking reuses it unchanged.

name: Fifteens are an ability
effect: Summing melds are too hard to see to be a default rule - they exist only when a card or rule card grants them.
note: Owner ruling. It is why The Fifteen is a rank and not a scoring default.

name: Rows poker columns runs
effect: Horizontal lines score as poker hands, vertical lines as runs. The two axes score differently on purpose.
note: The identity of the two score gutters. Diagonals and height lines inherit the row reading.

name: Elemental movement types
effect: Card materials with custom stack behaviour - one always floats to the top of its stack, one always sinks to the bottom of it.
note: Height turns the old deck-position gimmick into a board-position one.

name: Show end conditions
effect: A show ends when the deck runs out, when the fame goal is met, or when the player presses End.
note: End is now pressable at any time, which makes the deck-out case rare but not impossible.

name: Submit clears the board
effect: Submitting scored everything and swept the board, with the Entrance dropping down into the empty space.
note: SUPERSEDED - no sweep, no drop. A grid fills once and stays filled for the show.

name: Ascending or descending stacks
effect: The default stacking rule is adjacent rank and different suit, in either direction.
note: Implemented in the pip comparator; unchanged by the flip except that stacks now grow upward.

name: Vertical poker hands
effect: Grants columns the poker reading in addition to their run reading, so one column can score twice.
note: A rules card, not a default. It doubles a column's value and is priced for it.

name: Cards fall on their own
effect: Cards descended into the board automatically and could not be dragged there.
note: SUPERSEDED - placement is entirely by hand now, which is the whole point of the overhaul.

name: Top-down evaluation order
effect: Scoring walked the board a row at a time from the top so poker hands resolved before runs.
note: Mostly superseded: a line scores when it completes, so the player now chooses the order.

name: Rows times columns
effect: The two axes multiply rather than add.
note: Survives as the three-bucket product - row term times column term times special term, positive terms only.

name: Board state is an array
effect: The board is data, not nodes - a flat cell array with a coordinate, never a scene-tree walk.
note: Now GridData with a four-component coordinate. The reason the geometry can be pure arithmetic.

name: Trigger dispatch order
effect: Effects fire in one fixed order - field, deck top-down, then board left-to-right top-down including the Entrance, then discard newest first.
note: Now walks every grid in turn. The iterator's order is a contract the tests pin.

name: Simultaneous lane scoring
effect: All five lanes of a row were scored at once, returning the set of scored cards for the effect loop.
note: Superseded in timing, kept in shape - a completed line still returns one section of cards.

name: Elevated card list
effect: Scoring returns the list of cards that should visibly rise.
note: Still true, and the rise is now a spring up the stack rather than a hop.

name: Hop and shake on trigger
effect: Triggered cards hop and shake, and the triggering card is shown in the preview so the player can see what fired.
note: Implemented. The spring lift replaced the hop on the grid because cards now hang from their bottom edge.

name: Triangle draft map
effect: Choosing one of three cards moved the player up a tier and permanently closed the other lanes.
note: SUPERSEDED by the tour graph, which the worldgen addon already renders.

name: Boss phases as terrain
effect: Every few tiers is a boss node, drawn as terrain rather than as a card.
note: Survives into the tour as the city-versus-town distinction.

name: Tilted viewport map
effect: Render the 2D map to a viewport and tilt it for a cheap 3D table look.
note: Cheap, and the picture-wall camera already does the equivalent trick.

name: Axis-marked score labels
effect: Row scores and column scores are visually distinguished so the player can read which axis paid.
note: Now solved by position instead of punctuation - rows in the left gutter, columns below, specials to the right.

name: Poker Hand of the Four Above
effect: When this card scores, it and the four cards above it in its stack are also scored as a poker hand.
note: The card that most wants height to exist. Dead on a flat board, excellent on a tall one.

name: Every Fifth Card
effect: Every five cards down a column are read as an extra poker hand.
note: Long-column play; only reachable once a grid is stacked above height four.

name: Spiderweb
effect: Scores one point per card diagonally adjacent to it and again per card orthogonally adjacent - a cross laid over an X.
note: The purest placement card in the notes and the reason diagonals got their own bucket.

name: Skill taxonomy
effect: Skills are classified by verb - score, reposition, amplify, rewrite rules, manipulate the deck, cull, alter other skills, persist, spawn minigames, create temporary cards, cost something.
note: The classification the catalog's groups column encodes. Any new skill should land in one of these.

name: Score verbs
effect: New ways to score - new melds, new geometries, new buckets.
note: The largest and most inflationary family; the three-bucket product is what keeps it bounded.

name: Reposition verbs
effect: Ways to move cards after placement - swap, slide, launch, wrap, cross grids.
note: The grid made this family enormous, because a coordinate now means something.

name: Amplify verbs
effect: Ways to increase the points existing cards already produce.
note: Multiplicative effects need the tightest costing; they compound with everything.

name: Rule-change verbs
effect: Cards that edit the rule deck itself - stacking legality, meld legality, placement legality.
note: The most powerful family and the reason the rule deck is hidden by default.

name: Deck-manipulation verbs
effect: Ways to see, order, fetch or plant cards in the draw deck.
note: Information is power in a game where placement is committed.

name: Cull verbs
effect: Ways to remove cards you no longer want from the deck.
note: Thinning is the economy's other half; the shop pays in cards for exactly this reason.

name: Meta-effect verbs
effect: Cards that change how other skills work rather than doing anything themselves.
note: Echoing Trigger is the shipped example. They multiply testing cost, so keep them few.

name: Persistence verbs
effect: Effects that survive into the next show.
note: Carried by RunState rather than GameData; the boundary is the save format's.

name: Minigame verbs
effect: Cards that open a small self-contained game inside the show.
note: Deferred by the recommendations as system multiplication; the event nodes host them instead.

name: Temporary-card verbs
effect: Cards that create cards which do not survive the show.
note: The mirror-deck blind is the biggest single user of this family.

name: Priced-card verbs
effect: Cards whose power is paid for with an ongoing cost rather than a purchase price.
note: White Elephant is the archetype. The blind weights borrow the same idea.

name: Dot-art star flow
effect: Background of drifting dot-art starfield behind the picture wall.
note: Cheap parallax that does not compete with card art; the warm-foreground rule keeps it cold.

name: Guaranteed early draw
effect: Cards acquired this show are guaranteed to appear in the first Entrance refills of the next show.
note: Solves the bought-it-never-saw-it problem that makes shops feel bad.

name: Score swirl
effect: At show end the board's cards swirl up and dissolve into the score numerals as they tally.
note: The end-of-show payoff moment, now that scoring itself is spread across the whole show.

name: Null card
effect: Occupies a cell and highlights on hover, but has no rank or suit and scores nothing.
note: Spatial filler that teaches that position is not points. Also the enemy of the empty-tile blind objective.

name: 2D graphics study
effect: Reference talk on 2D game graphics, kept as art-direction source.
note: Reference only.

name: Prototype checklist
effect: The original prototype list - menu, settings, map, match-to-match flow, escalating goal, deck viewer, deck maker, saving.
note: Almost entirely shipped; kept as the record of what the first milestone was.

name: Balatro-shaped settings
effect: Menu and settings modelled on Balatro's until there is a reason to differ.
note: Shipped.

name: Star-wars card scroll
effect: Card choices scroll away downward as they are picked, spawning more above.
note: The pack-opening presentation; still unbuilt and still wanted.

name: Match-to-map return
effect: Finishing a show returns to the map with the run state intact.
note: Shipped through RunManager.

name: Escalating goal
effect: Each show raises the fame needed to clear the next.
note: Shipped. The goal-curve refit is still open as its own phase.

name: BigNumber scores
effect: Scores exceed 64-bit range, so every score container is a mantissa-exponent BigNumber.
note: Shipped, and invisible to duplicate_deep - every score container needs a hand-written copy.

name: Deck viewer
effect: Hovering the deck opens a viewer that builds card visuals lazily as you scroll, so a huge deck never loads at once.
note: Shipped, including the lazy build.

name: Future-card preview
effect: Show the next cards to be drawn above the Entrance slots rather than inside the deck viewer.
note: Still wanted; the Entrance is the right place because that is where the decision is made.

name: Deck viewer sorter
effect: Sort the deck viewer by rank, suit, class or trigger.
note: The trigger sort is the one that matters - it answers what will fire from the deck.

name: Deck maker
effect: A deck editor for building test decks, later exposed as a prestige unlock.
note: Shipped as a tool; the player-facing unlock is still meta-layer work.

name: Saving
effect: The run and the show both survive being closed mid-play.
note: Shipped. The grid's score buckets pack into parallel float and int arrays to do it.

name: Visible-to-trigger
effect: A skill fires only while its card is unblocked - the Spotlight.
note: Shipped. Height stacking made covering a real decision instead of an accident.

name: Hidden trigger
effect: Fires while covered.
note: Shipped as StampRevealing.

name: Deck trigger display
effect: A card triggering from inside the deck animates above the deck slot so the player can see it happen.
note: Without this, deck triggers are invisible and read as bugs.

name: First hand only
effect: Only the first poker hand scored in a line counts; later ones are ignored.
note: A restriction card, priced as a downside that another card pays you to run.

name: Any card may be placed here
effect: This card accepts any card on top of it regardless of stacking legality.
note: The stacking rules are modifiable by design; this is the simplest possible proof of it.

name: Hungry Hippo
effect: Consumes any card dropped onto it and adds that card's rank to its own, up to a cap.
note: Shipped as SkillHungryHippo. The cap is what keeps it from eating a whole grid.

name: Moving elemental types
effect: Card materials that relocate themselves on the board between placements rather than in the deck.
note: The grid gives this a coordinate to move along at last.

name: Ring banding
effect: Every fifth row is drawn in a warmer band so depth is readable at a glance.
note: Ties the visual to the performance-ring scoring bands.

name: Depth multiplier
effect: Points increase with the layer they are scored on - the higher the line, the larger the band multiplier.
note: The reward for stacking upward, and the counterweight to covering your own skills.

name: Only first poker hand
effect: A line scores only its single best hand.
note: Shipped as SkillEvalPokerBest - it is the default evaluator, not a variant.

name: Score from deck and discard
effect: Scoring also considers cards in the deck and the discard, not only the board.
note: A rules card. Global by definition, and one reason effect scope had to become explicit.

name: Every card on the map
effect: Every card in the game appears somewhere on the tour map as an obtainable node.
note: Turns the map into the collection screen; strong pull for the completion loop.

name: Quests
effect: Per-run objectives in the TFT sense, granting rewards mid-run.
note: Deferred by the recommendations as system multiplication - the blind objectives absorbed the idea.

name: Self-upgrading cards
effect: A card that permanently becomes a stronger version of itself once a condition is met during the run.
note: The draft asks whether this differs from an effect at all - it does not, except in presentation, which is the point.

name: Pip comparator
effect: One resolver class decides every pip-versus-pip interaction, gathering allow and deny votes into a whitelist and a blacklist.
note: Shipped as PipComparator. A deny beats an allow.

name: Pip visual classes
effect: Each pip owns its visuals as well as its rules, so a new suit is one class.
note: Shipped. Adding a suit is genuinely one file.

name: Stacking by resolver
effect: The comparator decides stacking legality by collecting every allow and every deny across the board; one deny beats every allow.
note: Shipped. The blacklist-wins rule is what makes restriction cards reliable.

name: Pips carry their own scoring
effect: A pip class may add static scoring methods of its own, so a new suit can bring a new meld with it rather than editing the evaluator.
note: The extension point that keeps the evaluator from growing a branch per suit.

name: Pip effects are always live
effect: A pip's effect is permanently active and is not gated by the Spotlight; only skills are.
note: Owner ruling. It is why suit props fire from covered cards but skills do not.

name: Wild pip
effect: Its own pip class that remembers the last pip it copied and behaves as that until it recopies.
note: Tracking the previous pip inside itself is what makes it deterministic across an undo.

name: Chameleon pip
effect: Chooses itself at random from the pips already present in its own row, its own column, or the whole grid.
note: Grid-local by construction - the sample set is the grid. Needs a re-roll rule pinned so undo is stable.

name: Cycling pip visuals
effect: A wild pip animates through the faces it could be, settling on the one it currently is.
note: The visual has to update on every board revision, which is why it rides the revision counter.

name: Stacking first pips later
effect: Get the stacking and scoring resolver right before designing exotic pips; the resolver is what makes exotic pips cheap.
note: Vindicated - the comparator shipped first and every pip since has been one file.

name: Deterministic randomness
effect: Every random draw comes from a seeded stream the engine cannot perturb, so a replay reproduces exactly.
note: Non-negotiable for undo, resume and seed sharing. Seed offsets must themselves be seeded.

name: Show-all-actives button
effect: A half-open eye button that opens fully and pushes covering cards aside so every active card's art is visible.
note: Disabled while a stack is held. The alternative - glow only - is cheaper and may be enough.

name: Compress-board button
effect: Collapses the whole board into a flavourless sheet - pips and skill names only, dimmed when inactive - so a tall board can be read at a glance.
note: The tall-stack readability answer. Picking up a stack in this mode lifts a stiff column.

name: Exchange Voucher
effect: Usable from inside the deck - swap it with any card currently on screen.
note: Global, and one of the few cards that acts while undrawn.

name: Every button is a card
effect: Shop rerolls, End, and every other button are themselves cards played on a board.
note: The strongest diegetic idea in the notes and the one with the largest UI cost.

name: Right-click to cue
effect: Cueing a card is a right click; cued cards carry a glowing border that clears when the last charge is spent.
note: Rotation is unavailable in a grid cell, so the border does the work a tap rotation would.

name: No node parenting
effect: Cards are not scene-tree children of the cards below them; the stack is data and the view derives position from it.
note: Shipped, and it is why a stack can spring, ease and reveal without fighting inherited transforms.

name: Sin of Gluttony
effect: Uncapped Hungry Hippo - feeds from anywhere including the deck and the discard, and never returns what it eats.
note: Global because it reaches into the deck. The uncapped rank is the whole card, so it must cost accordingly.

name: Uniqueness multiplier
effect: The multiplier rises by one for every distinct effect triggered, not for every trigger.
note: Shipped as the combo class set. It is the anti-hyperfocus lever the whole economy leans on.

name: Static texture table
effect: One static class holds every sheet and its frame layout so art lookups never go through the filesystem twice.
note: Shipped.

name: The Rule Deck
effect: A deck the player cannot see that holds one card per default rule - stacking, scoring, zone creation, grid allotment.
note: Shipped and load-bearing. Changing the game is changing its cards.

name: Default stacking card
effect: The rule card that defines legal stacking. Remove it and nothing may be stacked at all.
note: Shipped.

name: Default scoring card
effect: The rule card that defines which melds score. Replacing it is how a deck changes the whole scoring vocabulary.
note: Shipped as the poker evaluator plus the line detector.

name: Rule deck metagame
effect: Over a run the player adds cards to and removes cards from the rule deck, permanently changing that run's game.
note: The long-term content engine. Ascensions and blinds are both writes to this deck.

name: Boss effects are rule cards
effect: A blind is a temporary card added to the rule deck, defined as destroying itself when the show ends.
note: The whole blinds category rides on this - no new system, just cards with a lifetime.

name: The Universal Deck
effect: Names considered for the rule deck - Universal, Fundamental, Rule.
note: Rule Deck won in the code. Keep one name.

name: Vouchers go in the play deck
effect: Voucher-style permanent upgrades sit in the main deck rather than the rule deck, so they can be drawn and seen.
note: Keeps the rule deck for rules and the play deck for cards.

name: Label type
effect: A rule card carrying this type announces its effect on the board even while the rule deck is invisible.
note: Baba-is-you legibility. Without it, hidden rules read as bugs.

name: Everything is a card
effect: Every rule, button, hazard and zone in the game is a card with modifiers.
note: The second pillar. It is why blinds cost almost nothing to add.

name: Rule deck resolves last
effect: The rule deck is the final collection in dispatch order, so rules see what every card has already done.
note: Shipped. A rule that resolved first could not react to the board it governs.

name: Rule cards carry pips
effect: Rule cards are given a random rank and suit so they behave sanely if an effect ever pulls one onto the board.
note: Cheap insurance against a card with no pips reaching a scoring line.

name: Decks as solitaire boards
effect: Every deck would itself be a small solitaire board the player could play to reorder or extract rules.
note: VETOED in the draft - the player cannot lay out those boards, so most would be unsolvable.

name: Immutable card anatomy
effect: A card always has a suit, a rank, a stamp slot, a skill slot and a type. Nothing removes those slots.
note: Shipped. The flip moved where they are drawn, not what they are.

name: One parent one child
effect: A card has at most one card below it and one above it, which is what makes a stack a list.
note: Shipped, and the reason height is a single integer rather than a tree.

name: Immutable collections
effect: The board, the draw deck, the discard and the rule deck always exist; only their contents change.
note: Now the board is a list of grids plus the Entrance rather than two zones.

name: Layout parsed from rules
effect: The board's shape is read out of the rule deck at game creation, not hard-coded.
note: Shipped as SkillGridAllotment plus SkillGridCreator - deck size decides grid count.

name: Scoring section is not a card
effect: The scoring section itself stays engine-side; only what it evaluates is card-driven.
note: Owner ruling with an explicit escape hatch - functionality that can be duplicated or removed may become a card.

name: Entrance cards are abilities
effect: Even the Entrance slots are cards whose skill hands their contents to the board and draws a replacement.
note: Shipped as TypeInput. Five of them, one per column.

name: Dynamic column count
effect: The number of Entrance slots and board columns is decided by counting rule cards, so five is a default and not a constant.
note: Effects must never assume five. The grid tests sweep ragged widths for exactly this reason.

name: Linked trigger card
effect: Cue this card to force the card it is stacked with to trigger, whatever that card's own condition is.
note: Turns conditional effects into on-demand ones, which is powerful enough to want a charge limit.

name: Rulesets pack
effect: An unlockable card pack whose contents are rule cards rather than performers.
note: The endgame pack. Only sensible once the rule deck is visible to the player.

name: Custom rule decks
effect: A rule deck expressive enough to rebuild classic solitaire inside the game.
note: Acknowledged scope creep in the draft itself; kept as an aspiration, not a milestone.

name: Prestige points
effect: Wins grant points spent in a between-run menu to shift card and event odds, or to take debuffs for more points.
note: Vampire Survivors' shape. Overlaps ascensions, so the two need one shared currency or none.

name: Charge halo
effect: A cueable card wears a halo divided by black gaps into as many segments as it has charges remaining.
note: Fixed radius, changing divisions - readable at a glance without a number.

name: Eye stamp art
effect: The always-active stamp shows a miniature of the skill's own art inside the eye, so a covered card still says what it does.
note: Small, and it removes a tooltip.

name: Rules-in-the-deck variant
effect: A starting deck whose rule deck is empty because every rule card has been shuffled into the play deck.
note: Chaos deck. Every rule is drawable, discardable and stealable.

name: Packs on the map
effect: Map nodes hold card packs rather than single cards, and the map may have holes in it.
note: Packs beat singles for pacing - a choice inside a choice.

name: The card spreadsheet
effect: One spreadsheet holds every card - title, rarity, cost in cards, description, tags.
note: This file's ancestor. The catalog now carries the grid axes as well.

name: Rarity borders
effect: Rarer cards carry different borders and different shine treatments, holographic at the top end.
note: Cheap perceived value; the shader work is already in the FX plan.

name: Power-sorted chains
effect: Design a common base effect, then print stronger versions of it as separate cards; rarity is where a card sits on its own chain.
note: Makes rarity mean something measurable instead of a vibe.

name: Stack-payment shop
effect: Cards for sale sit above; the price is a stack of cards drawn from your deck below, and paying removes them.
note: Makes thinning and buying the same action. Reroll prices climb per use.

name: Progression systems essay
effect: Progression systems retain players whether or not money is involved; go deep on few systems rather than wide on many.
note: The owner's own brake on system multiplication. Cite it before adding a system.

name: QOL for time sinks
effect: Add convenience to the parts that cost time rather than to the parts that are fun.
note: The rule that justifies the compress-board and show-actives buttons.

name: Card unlocks
effect: Common cards unlock on generic progress; rare cards unlock on specific deeds, tracked on one shared pass so order never matters.
note: The order-independent pass is the good idea here - it removes checklist anxiety.

name: Prestige spending
effect: Prestige buys odds changes, extra rerolls, starting cards, true vision of the rule deck, and eventually a custom deck editor.
note: Odds manipulation is the version that respects the map; flat power is the version that does not.

name: Deck unlocks
effect: Unlockable starting decks that double as the gimmick-run mode rather than living in a separate tab.
note: Folding gimmick runs into decks avoids a whole second progression surface.

name: Ascensions
effect: Each ascension adds one negative card to the run's deck or rule deck - the permanent home for retired hazard cards.
note: Ascension cards and blind cards are the same object with different lifetimes.

name: Lore and secrets
effect: Wins unlock scraps of lore and cosmetics; secrets need no answer to drive engagement.
note: Deferred, but secrets are cheap - the Erdnase cipher costs one signature field.

name: Eye of God
effect: Reveals every deck and every true description including the rule deck.
note: Global. The information ceiling of the game, and a prestige unlock in card form.

name: Hand of God
effect: Move any card to any coordinate on any grid, and reorder the draw deck at will.
note: The four-coordinate move in one card. Needs a charge limit or it plays the game for you.

name: Foot of God
effect: Swap this card's position with any other card on screen, including cards in other grids and the Entrance.
note: The cheapest of the three because a swap preserves the board's card count.

name: Third eye motif
effect: The god trio can be drawn as third eye, third hand and third foot rather than as deities.
note: Keeps the circus register - a sideshow prodigy, not a pantheon.

name: Community channel
effect: Ship a direct community link in the game, as Balatro did, and manage the community personally.
note: Reference only, no mechanic.

name: Exponential cost curve
effect: Card cost rises slower than card power, because flexibility is part of a card's budget - cheap cards must stay weak because they always fit.
note: The costing rule the catalog's cost column should be audited against.

name: Scoring contextualises everything
effect: Scoring is the most important system because it tells every other card what to aim at.
note: The argument for settling the economy before printing more cards.

name: Score as damage
effect: Reframe points as damage against the audience so that effects read as attacks.
note: Adopted as framing only - the audience is the antagonist and the goal score is its health.

name: Effects are points melds are mult
effect: Card effects supply the flat points; row and column melds supply the multipliers.
note: The combo reframe. It is why a board with no effects scores honestly low.

name: Avalanche
effect: At show end every card left on the board attacks the goal, reducing the fame required by one per card.
note: Attacks the target instead of the total - the only card that moves the goalpost.

name: Static stylised look
effect: Less 3D motion, no idle hover except a slow side-to-side; 3D reserved for special cases, with the budget spent on sound instead.
note: The direction the flip followed. Cards still feel alive, through sound and anticipation.

name: Card art as background
effect: The background is built from the art of the cards currently in play.
note: Free variety, and it makes a deck feel like a troupe.

name: Status array
effect: Cards carry a status dictionary of name to value, processed by a rule card rather than by the card itself.
note: Shipped for Burning and Juggling. Injury and Exhaust want the same slot.

name: Game-laws button
effect: A question-mark button that shows the rules; greyed out with a hint until the player has earned rule-deck vision.
note: Teases the rule deck before revealing it - the mystery is the point.

name: Cards rise while attacking
effect: Every card rises and hovers while a score is being resolved.
note: The show-is-happening state. Cheap and legible.

name: Tornado into the deck
effect: At show end every card everywhere spirals back into the draw deck.
note: Closes the loop visually and hides the state reset.

name: Crunchy sound and cursor attraction
effect: Inscryption-style crunch on every interaction; cards lean slightly toward the cursor and active cards breathe.
note: The compensation for cutting 3D motion.

name: Data drives view
effect: One data layer feeds both the UI layer and the card layer; the view never holds truth.
note: Shipped, and it is why the grid geometry could become pure arithmetic over cached inputs.

name: Party effects
effect: Confetti, streamers and crowd noise scaled to the size of the score.
note: The applause curve. Bigger scores earn louder rooms.

name: Effect art pop-up
effect: When an effect fires, its art blooms in the background as though the act were being performed.
note: The single strongest juice idea in the notes; it makes a trigger feel like a performance.

name: Grand Entrance and The Ring
effect: The upper zone is the Grand Entrance and the play board is The Ring.
note: Shipped in the vocabulary. The Entrance is row -1 of whichever grid it is attached to.

name: Performers and feats
effect: Cards are performers, skills are feats, the player is the Ringmaster.
note: Shipped in the vocabulary.

name: Fame and tips
effect: Scoring excites the audience; the goal is fame and overscoring earns tips.
note: The rename that turns a number into a fiction without changing a formula.

name: Circus suits
effect: The suits are clowns, dancers, flames, juggling balls, hoops and knives, with aces as the headline performers.
note: Settled at four base suits plus specials; clowns and dancers became classes instead.

name: Traveling troupe menu
effect: The main menu is the troupe's wagon between towns.
note: Diegetic menu that costs one scene.

name: Circus skills index
effect: The Wikipedia list of circus skills as the source index for feat names.
note: Reference only; DESIGN_REFERENCES.md supersedes it with sourced detail.

name: Performance rings
effect: Scores are banded by ring - the first five rows score once over, the next band twice over, and so on outward.
note: The reward for building outward and upward. Now expressed as a height band multiplier.

name: Three acts
effect: Three submits per show, themed as three acts.
note: SUPERSEDED - a show is one continuous performance that ends when the player presses End.

name: Leader cards
effect: Starts the show already on the board or in the Entrance and does not leave when a line scores.
note: The deck's face. Its survival rule is the only thing that makes it structurally different.

name: The Ringmaster
effect: No suit and no rank; starts in the Entrance, may always be picked up, may be placed anywhere with nothing on top, and stays after scoring.
note: The tutorial leader. Its rulelessness is what teaches the rules.

name: Flavour debuffs
effect: Leaders may carry a phobia - a fear of flames or knives that forbids placing them on that suit.
note: Makes a leader a constraint as well as a bonus, which is what stops leaders being pure upside.

name: Leaders define decks
effect: Each starting deck ships a different leader, and the leader is the build the deck wants.
note: The cleanest identity hook the game has.

name: Magician class
effect: Card creation and deletion.
note: Class taxonomy. Global by nature - it writes to collections rather than to cells.

name: Acrobat class
effect: Card movement across the grid and up and down stacks.
note: Class taxonomy. The class the fourth coordinate most enlarged.

name: Animal Trainer class
effect: Stacking, eating, and cards that move themselves around the field.
note: Class taxonomy.

name: Clown class
effect: Pip manipulation - changing ranks and suits after placement.
note: Class taxonomy. The fixer class that rescues a mis-placed line.

name: Dancer class
effect: Formation focus - effects that care about the shape cards make rather than their values.
note: Class taxonomy. The class that most needs the diagonal bucket.

name: Escape Artist class
effect: Negative effects, insurance, and getting out of them.
note: Class taxonomy. The counterplay class blinds exist to give work to.

name: Fortune Teller class
effect: Deck manipulation and information.
note: Class taxonomy. Global by definition.

name: Special Effects class
effect: Points and combo manipulation - the fireworks family.
note: Class taxonomy. The most inflationary class, so cost it hardest.

name: Concessions class
effect: Positive effects, buffs and food.
note: Class taxonomy.

name: Costume Designer class
effect: Equipment, clothing and stamps.
note: Class taxonomy. The class that edits other cards rather than the board.

name: Producer class
effect: Token cards - gold, basics, and the machinery of paying for things.
note: Class taxonomy.

name: Group synergy
effect: Cards belong to groups and a leader boosts its own group; a group in one grid is what an effect counts.
note: The autochess import lands here - copies of a class in one grid scale that class's effect.

name: Hats not stamps
effect: Rename stamps as hats, or as costume pieces generally.
note: Stamp stayed in the code; hat is the player-facing word. One extra slot type was judged overkill.

name: Type taxonomy
effect: Types are structural - materials, deck behaviour and act ordering.
note: Distinct from skills, which are effects, and stamps, which modify a card.

name: First Act type
effect: Appears alone in the Entrance before any other card is drawn.
note: Guaranteed opener. Turns one card into a plan.

name: Second Act type
effect: Appears alone once half the deck has been drawn.
note: A midpoint pivot the player can build toward.

name: Final Act type
effect: Appears alone after every other card has been drawn.
note: The closer. Pairs with any end-of-show payout effect.

name: Presentation-stage preview
effect: The card preview is a lit stage - the text scrolls, the card does not.
note: Shipped. Keeps the card still so the art can be read.

name: Attraction packs
effect: Card packs are attractions, not expansions.
note: Vocabulary.

name: Cue not tap
effect: Activating a card is cueing it.
note: Vocabulary. The code still says trigger; the player sees cue.

name: Peeking skills
effect: A covered card with a skill idly leans out from under the card above it.
note: Makes covered-but-active visible without a UI element.

name: Half-art visibility
effect: A covered active card is offset enough that at least the upper half of its art shows.
note: The reveal offset. Implemented as the reveal stack in the grid layout.

name: Carnival meta shop
effect: The between-run hub is a carnival midway.
note: Renamed Winter Quarters in the recommendations, which is the better history.

name: Suit props
effect: A scored basic card spawns props of its suit, count from its rank, which travel its scored row or column and interact with what they pass.
note: Shipped for all four base suits. The single best-realised idea in the notes.

name: Prop travel axes
effect: Knives and hoops travel horizontally along the scored row; balls and flames fall down the column.
note: Shipped. The axis split is what makes suit choice a placement decision.

name: Prop interaction table
effect: Hoops pay for passing talents, knives pay for missing them, balls buff talents, flames buff everything else.
note: Shipped. Two suits reward a talent-rich row and two reward a talent-poor one.

name: Fireworks suit
effect: A firework rises up its column and banks points into the column directly, scaled by its rank.
note: Shipped as PipSuitFirework. The only suit that scores without a prop interaction.

name: Prop balance split
effect: Horizontal props are chosen at random between knives and hoops so a row cannot be farmed by one suit.
note: The balance note behind the shipped split; keep it when adding a fifth suit.

name: Living feat cards
effect: Feat cards should be alive and individually animated, since props physically interact with them.
note: The art budget that props imply. Prop-art verification is its own gate.

name: Jump and duck
effect: Cards jump to pass through a hoop and duck under a passing knife.
note: Shipped. It is what makes the prop pass legible rather than decorative.

name: Electric suit
effect: Buffs cards connected to it in an unbroken chain, following adjacency through height as well as across the grid.
note: The suit that most wants the fourth coordinate. Chain length is its rank equivalent.

name: Reuse card art
effect: Reuse art aggressively across cards rather than commissioning one image per card.
note: The constraint that keeps a 400-card catalog affordable.

name: Game laws as text
effect: Before the rule deck is unlocked, the rules are readable as plain text so prop behaviour can be explained at all.
note: Necessary - prop rules are invisible otherwise.

name: Prop cards
effect: A card with no feat is a prop card; props are what knives miss and hoops ignore.
note: Vocabulary, and a real mechanical class - the knife and hoop split keys off it.

name: Odds buying raises the goal
effect: Prestige spending that improves your odds also raises the fame each show demands - more attractions draw a bigger crowd.
note: The self-balancing prestige system. It is the reason prestige can be generous.

name: Optimisation essay
effect: A deckbuilder chasing one rising number collapses into hyperfocus, and the most fun stretch is before the deck is optimal.
note: The argument blinds answer. Keep it in view when costing any multiplicative card.

name: Formation win conditions
effect: Alternate win conditions built on formations do not scale - flushes have a hard ceiling, and a good enough deck guarantees them.
note: Measured dead end. It is why objectives became per-level blinds rather than run-long win conditions.

name: Blinds as resilience tests
effect: Negative level effects test whether a deck can handle anything, punishing hyperfocus the way Slay the Spire enemies do.
note: The founding argument for the blinds category. Every blind should threaten a different pillar.

name: Towns with tastes
effect: Each town has a taste - knifetown is unimpressed by knife melds and pays nothing for them, and the same for fire, juggling and hoops.
note: The suit-resistance family. Four blinds from one idea, each hitting a different deck.

name: Funnelled routes
effect: Limit how freely the player can dodge hazards by funnelling the route through mountains and forests.
note: The counter to hazard-shopping. Without it, blinds become optional.

name: Reroll grants irreversibility
effect: Grants an extra reroll, and for the rest of the show a repeated action never gives the same result twice.
note: A drawback that is also a fantasy - the show cannot be rehearsed.

name: One-way activation
effect: Once switched on, an effect stays on for the rest of the show and cannot be switched off again.
note: Removes toggle micro-management and makes activation a decision instead of a routine.

name: Spotlight naming
effect: Active is renamed Spotlight - an unblocked card is in the spotlight.
note: Shipped in the vocabulary and the code.

name: Spotlight icon in text
effect: Every description states whether its trigger needs the spotlight, so cards that fire regardless are obvious.
note: Without this the spotlight is invisible rules. It also devalues the always-active stamp, which is fine.

name: Zone expand on hover
effect: Hovering a held stack over a zone expanded the zone control, pushing the cards below down.
note: SUPERSEDED - a grid cell is a fixed slot, and the row grows only when a stack actually gets taller.

name: Narrow drag controls
effect: Card controls are narrower than the card art so the board behind can still be grabbed and panned.
note: Now solved by the pan and zoom modes instead; kept as an input note.

name: Cannon-fired background
effect: Card art from every card in play is fired across the background from cannons at the screen edges, fruit-ninja style.
note: Ties the background to the deck without a second art pass.

name: Double Everything deck
effect: Ranks are doubled, which doubles the deck, which doubles the Entrance slots, the grids and the fame required.
note: The grid allotment rule makes this nearly free - a doubled deck simply unlocks more grids.

name: Slot-machine pack opening
effect: A pack opening shows every card the pack could have contained behind the ones it did, reel-style; results stay seed-fixed.
note: Near-miss presentation, the strongest reinforcement schedule available. Show what you almost pulled.

name: No single digits
effect: Never show a single-digit score - big numbers are the genre's language.
note: The reason BigNumber exists and the reason base scores start in the tens.

name: Custom deck as endgame
effect: The deck editor is the last unlock, not the first.
note: Protects the discovery curve; a custom deck answers questions the player has not asked yet.

name: Goofy travel animations
effect: Cards spin and bounce across the screen when an effect moves them, and slot into place like a filing drawer.
note: Cross-grid moves are long journeys now, which makes this more valuable than it was.

name: Cards are alive
effect: Every motion choice should support the idea that cards are performers, not tokens.
note: The direction that survived the cut of 3D motion.

name: Mana cards
effect: Any card can be spent as a resource, as in Magic, instead of a mana bar.
note: Deferred - the game already pays for things in cards at the shop, and two card economies is one too many.

name: Mystery Box
effect: At show start, becomes a random skill for that show.
note: The cheapest variance card. Its value is the reroll, not the payoff.

name: Pandora Box
effect: At show start becomes a random skill; at show end reverts to Pandora Box.
note: Same card with the reset stated, so it never becomes permanently good or permanently dead.

name: Utter Chaos
effect: Becomes a different random skill on every Entrance refill.
note: The refill is the new heartbeat, so this rerolls several times a show.

name: Escalating act multiplier
effect: Each act multiplied harder than the last, with the final act worth most.
note: SUPERSEDED with acts. The height band multiplier took over the same job spatially.

name: Card debuffs
effect: Cards accumulate lasting debuffs - Exhausted loses rank at show end if it was on the board.
note: The status dictionary already supports it. Blinds are the natural source.

name: Reward speed with cards
effect: Rewarding a fast win risks rewarding min-maxing, so pay for speed in cards and buffs rather than in score.
note: Owner's own correction. Keep speed rewards off the score axis.

name: Cheat Day
effect: At show end, every card still in the draw deck gains a rank.
note: Rewards ending early, which is exactly the pressure the End button needs.

name: Rarity chain cards
effect: A common card that doubles the chance of rares, and so on up the chain.
note: VETOED by the recommendations - dead cards that only touch the meta layer and fight the cards-as-currency economy.

name: Level rules
effect: Rules specific to one level, standing in for the rule deck - needed for shop levels and hazard levels.
note: Settled as blinds written into the rule deck rather than a separate level deck, which would be scope creep.

name: Global rule type
effect: A card type whose skill is always in the global spotlight, which is what makes a rule card a rule card.
note: Makes rule cards ordinary cards with one type, so a player can eventually hold one.

name: Homing types
effect: Types that return a card to a named deck when something happens to it.
note: The mechanism behind consumables that come back and blinds that expire.

name: Selection override
effect: Selecting a card must be overridable by effects, since what a click does is itself a rule.
note: Shipped through the grabber and placer rule cards.

name: Carry-over scoring
effect: Points banked outside the main show carry into the next one.
note: Lives on RunState. The Storyteller card is the player-facing version.

name: Buttons defined by rules
effect: What the End button does is defined by the rule deck, so a scenario can redefine it and the change persists for the run.
note: Shipped in shape - End now only fires hooks, which is itself a rule card decision.

name: Genie scenario
effect: Make a wish - copy any one card into your deck on the spot.
note: The wish framing lets an event grant something huge without breaking the shop economy.

name: Flexible game class
effect: The game class must host scenarios that differ in board, rules and buttons without forking.
note: Vindicated by the grid overhaul, which reused the class wholesale.

name: Retire button
effect: A settings button that ends a run early and banks whatever the run earned.
note: Removes the dead-run slog. Cheap and kind.

name: Storyteller
effect: Preserves a portion of this show's score into the next one.
note: The clean way to make a lost show still worth playing out.

name: Score screen shake
effect: Scoring shakes the screen, and a large score pans the camera onto the cards and away from the buttons.
note: Now doubly useful - the board is wide, so a pan is already the camera's language.

name: Retirement condition
effect: A card cannot be retired from the deck until it has scored or triggered at least once.
note: Stops instant culling of every card the player did not immediately understand.

name: Shared charge system
effect: Every effect with charges draws on one shared charge system, so any source can add or spend charges on anything.
note: One system, many cards. Unspent charges should carry into the next refill.

name: Pack mulligans
effect: A pack's contents can be rerolled arena-style rather than picked from, with a previewable pool and an upgradeable mulligan count.
note: Turns opening a pack into a small game with its own decisions.

name: Entrance mulligan card
effect: Cue to mulligan the Entrance, drawing a fresh set into the empty slots.
note: The card version of the free discard, and the reason the discard need not be free.

name: Upgraded pack results
effect: Pack results can roll upgraded, arriving with a bonus type or stamp already attached.
note: Needs its own viewer, since a card with two extra modifiers no longer reads at pack size.

name: Unseen effects hidden
effect: An effect the player has never seen shows as a question mark in the pack preview.
note: Preserves discovery without hiding the whole pack.

name: Loose rare on the map
effect: Some map nodes hold a single high-rarity card instead of a pack.
note: Route-planning bait, and a reason to detour.

name: Encounters as minigames
effect: Some encounters are small solitaire games in their own right.
note: Deferred with the other minigame ideas, but events are the right host.

name: Rooted cards
effect: A card that resists being moved by effects, its own or anyone's.
note: Rosin in the recommendations. Commitment in exchange for a bonus.

name: Info toggle
effect: Reading full descriptions needs a held button or an info toggle, because left and right click are already spoken for.
note: Middle click on mouse; the toggle is what controllers and touch use.

name: HONK
effect: Cue to honk. Unlimited uses. Does nothing else.
note: Sincerely worth printing - a free joke card teaches the cue verb painlessly.

name: Secret melds
effect: Melds that are not documented anywhere and are added to the rule deck by cards as they enter the deck.
note: The engagement engine. The 42-point meld from the recommendations is the model.

name: Disaster packs
effect: Packs on the board offering only negative cards, taken for a reward.
note: The ascension-card delivery mechanism, chosen rather than imposed.

name: Literal spotlights
effect: Actives are lit by an actual stage spotlight rather than a generic glow, with the rest of the board dimmed.
note: The theme and the mechanic finally being the same object.

name: Biome worlds
effect: The tour runs through biomes, each generating the map differently.
note: One Step From Eden's structure over the worldgen graph.

name: Fame gates
effect: Every ten levels the run demands a fame threshold to continue.
note: Umamusume's gate. A hard checkpoint that makes the wager decisions real.

name: Fog of war on the route
effect: The tour ahead is fogged, so only the nearest choices are legible.
note: The newest draft narrows this to seeing only as far as the closest city.

name: The show must go on
effect: Weather hazards are framed as adversity the troupe performs through rather than as punishment.
note: The tone rule for every negative blind - never say no, say harder.

name: Constellation tour map
effect: An FTL-style constellation map with no backtracking, threading cities around the world.
note: Shipped in shape by the worldgen graph.

name: Tour planning
effect: Before the run the player traces the intended route; longer routes unlock as tours are finished.
note: The Route Book. Deviating from the plan should cost fame.

name: Packs or singles as node rewards
effect: Every reward node offers either a pack or a rarer single card.
note: Two reward shapes is enough variety; three would blur.

name: Temporary prestige events
effect: An event grants prestige points to spend immediately, reusing the prestige screen mid-run.
note: Recycles a whole UI for one event type.

name: Consequence events
effect: Events fire based on what the run has done - sacrifice too many talents and the troupe strikes; hoard too many cards and the taxman calls.
note: Makes the run's history visible without a narrative system.

name: Puzzle events
effect: Events whose win condition is a puzzle rather than a score - trigger five times, fill one column, score nothing at all.
note: The same objective vocabulary the blinds use, pointed at a reward instead of a threat.

name: World tour structure
effect: Cross the world building fame; clearing a city raises the next city's requirement; the final city wins the run and unlocks endless.
note: The run's shape. Endless repeats the final city with guaranteed offers between shows.

name: Fame improves rarity
effect: Total fame raises the odds of better cards appearing.
note: Ties the score axis to the collection axis without a second currency.

name: Endless mode
effect: After the final city, repeat it until you lose, chasing a high score.
note: The score-attack outlet, which lets the main run stop being one.

name: Circular tour
effect: Instead of a final city, circle the map and return to the start once enough time has passed.
note: Alternative to the linear tour; makes revisits meaningful.

name: Maximum Effort stamp
effect: Doubles this card's points when it scores, then refuses to refresh unless the card sits out the next show entirely.
note: Glass-like risk with a rest mechanic rather than a destruction one.

name: Complexity gates
effect: The high scores that gate progress require either luck or genuinely complicated card chains, which pushes players toward dynamic decks.
note: The argument for large boards and long chains being the aspirational play.

name: Talent packs
effect: Booster packs are talent packs.
note: Vocabulary.

name: Discard as the engine
effect: Discarding from the Entrance repeatedly until the right cards appear is the main way a board gets built; the discard count is upgradeable.
note: The single biggest tempo lever. Start at one discard and sell more.

name: Procedural biome fill
effect: Fill the generated map's biomes with wave-function-collapse or min-conflicts after the towns are placed.
note: Towns first, scenery second - the route must be authored, the scenery need not be.

name: Extruded heightmap map
effect: Build the top-down 3D relief map from one flat biome image plus a heightmap through an extrude shader.
note: One image, one shader, a whole diorama. Slopes come from eroding one pixel per layer.

name: Forbidden solitaire event
effect: A click-to-stack solitaire variant used as an event minigame.
note: Small enough to be an event and not a mode.

name: Effect-order deck view
effect: The deck viewer shows the order effects will fire in even when the card order is hidden, using question-mark pips for anything that does not affect that.
note: Only shows cards that can trigger from the deck. Reveals the pip when only one card could be meant.

name: Rank-identified rule cards
effect: Duplicate rule cards are told apart by rank - zone adder one has rank one.
note: Shipped. It is how five identical Entrance cards stay addressable.

name: Free undo per turn
effect: One free undo per turn, not carried forward.
note: Baked in by default. Extra undos are earned, and going back in time must not re-grant them.

name: Biome unlocks
effect: Playing unlocks more biomes and longer possible routes.
note: Flagged in the draft as the Mewgenics problem - gating content behind grind. Endless mode is the mitigation.

name: Press Bribery
effect: An extra life - fail a city and continue as though you had won.
note: Saved for the end it is a guaranteed win, which is why it must be findable at most once.

name: Node preview
effect: Clicking a map node previews it; a separate button commits to travelling there.
note: Prevents the misclick that ends a run.

name: Own RNG
effect: Ship a hand-written generator the engine cannot change, with seeded per-stream offsets rather than one shared seed.
note: Correlated randomness is the failure mode; per-stream offsets are the fix.

name: The yak shave
effect: A run should seduce the player into abandoning their plan for a better one they did not expect.
note: The pivot loop. Every run wants one card that offers it.

name: Precomputed maps
effect: Generate maps on a background thread while the player is still in the menu, one per size.
note: Hides the only long load the run has.

name: Hype wager
effect: Choose to double the fame the next show demands in exchange for better rewards.
note: The Booking, in its simplest form. It is the alternative to bigger numbers.

name: Presentation card
effect: Moving cards in ascending rank order during one turn grants a multiplier.
note: Rewards the order of play rather than the final board, which nothing else does.

name: Guaranteed pack preview
effect: A map node shows at least one card the pack definitely contains.
note: Enough information to plan a route around, not enough to remove the surprise.

name: Branching campaign paths
effect: Themed paths of escalating levels, where clearing one path unlocks tools that help on another.
note: Battle Cats' structure. Splits cleanly into roguelike tours and authored puzzle levels.

name: Chess pawn
effect: Swaps with the card directly above it; from the bottom of a stack it may swap two up; a diagonal move upward captures.
note: The clearest use of height as a chess rank. Capture must swap rather than delete or one piece eats a grid.

name: Chess pieces
effect: Other pieces may move to any cell their chess movement allows, swapping with whatever is there.
note: Swap not capture, so the board's card count is preserved and the piece cannot run away with the show.

name: Chess king
effect: Moves one cell in any direction, never captures, and automatically flees any cell a chess card threatens; enormous points if it is ever captured.
note: An alternate win condition in card form, and the piece that makes the others tactical.

name: Freakshow class
effect: Every card whose rank is not an ordinary number belongs to the freakshow.
note: The home for Blank, Wild, Half-step, Roman and the negative ranks.

name: Digital type
effect: Cannot be discarded off the board once placed.
note: Anti-removal. Turns a good placement into a permanent one, for better and worse.

name: Audience patience
effect: The audience has a patience meter; moving cards spends it, triggering a new effect refunds some, and at zero the show ends.
note: Bounds a show in actions rather than turns and makes every move cost something.

name: Clown patience
effect: Each distinct clown card on the board raises maximum patience by one; a full set can spend a move for free.
note: The autochess set bonus, arriving before autochess was named as the source.

name: Patience display
effect: Patience shows as a bar, never as a fraction, so one remaining action reads as one.
note: A fraction invites an off-by-one misread; a bar does not.

name: Warm foreground
effect: Warm colours advance and cold recede, so the art is warm and the UI is cold.
note: The palette rule the whole interface obeys.

name: Mika Pikazo study
effect: The compiled technique list kept as the art-direction source for the card and background treatment.
note: Reference. The eight techniques below are the actionable half.

name: Street-art palette
effect: Hyper-saturated neon pinks, cyans and yellows to recreate the visual noise of street murals.
note: The maximal end of the palette. The Seuss fusion is the restrained alternative.

name: Chromatic aberration
effect: Split the RGB channels at the outer edges of the frame so the subject steps forward.
note: A frame effect, not a card effect - it belongs to the picture wall.

name: Chromatic contrast
effect: Pair colour-wheel opposites, hot magenta against bright cyan, to exploit how warm advances and cold recedes.
note: The same physics as the warm-foreground rule, applied within one image.

name: Hard-edge shading
effect: Sharp posterised shading with hard brushes across most of the artwork.
note: Cheap to author and it matches the flat card-art style already in the project.

name: Poster graphic punch
effect: Flat hard-edged shading reads as commercial poster art, which is exactly the circus lithograph register.
note: The style and the theme agree here, which is rare and worth exploiting.

name: Blending-mode glow
effect: Layer ultra-bright secondary colours into shadow borders so surfaces look self-illuminating, like neon signage.
note: The midway-at-night look. Cheap as a shader, expensive if hand-painted.

name: Reverse-contrast isolation
effect: Surround a flat, lightly shaded face with hyper-dense background detail so the eye rests on the face.
note: The reason card art can be simple while the background is busy - it is a feature, not a saving.

name: Rhythmic asymmetry
effect: Pack scenes with floating debris, geometry and halftones so a still image carries carnival motion.
note: Applies to the picture-wall frames more than to cards, which must stay readable at small size.

name: Canvas noise
effect: Overlay film grain, screen tone and analog texture at the frame edge.
note: Frame-level, so it costs one full-screen pass and never touches card legibility.

name: Neo-vintage fusion
effect: Pikazo's dense digital structure with a muted Dr Seuss ink palette - high fidelity, low saturation.
note: The chosen direction. Off-white ground, three or four muted flats, one unmuted accent.

name: Muted flat palette
effect: Avocado green, dusty mustard, soft sky blue on an off-white paper ground, with high-energy motion on top.
note: The palette entry the palette database should encode as a named ramp.

name: Seussian shading fit
effect: Seuss used flat unshaded fills inside ink lines, which suits hard-brush shading exactly - the result reads as silk-screened streetwear.
note: Why the two references combine instead of fighting.

name: Anachronistic aberration
effect: RGB splitting over a muted palette reads as a misregistered mid-century printing press rather than as an LED screen.
note: The same shader, a different century, because the palette changed. Good cheap flavour.

name: Amplified focus
effect: Desaturated backgrounds let the eye navigate dense composition faster, so chaos stops being overload.
note: The readability argument for the muted direction, which matters on a board of seventy-five cards.

name: Art execution formula
effect: Off-white ground, three or four flats, one iconic accent used only for eyes or one garment, crisp black outlines, hard-edged shading, aberration plus paper-fibre grain to finish.
note: The step-by-step brief any card commission should carry.

name: Film-grain transitions
effect: Scenes enter as grainy film that resolves into the real moment; transitions look like a film strip slowing then speeding up.
note: Undo becomes a rewind, and if new scenes arrive from above, undo arrives from below.

name: Record scratch
effect: A record-scratch sting on an illegal move or a cancelled action.
note: One sound that removes the need for an error message.

name: Undo accrual
effect: Undos accrue every few turns, tracked against the turn number they were earned at, so rewinding time cannot re-grant them.
note: The bookkeeping that stops undo farming; without it, going back is free power.

name: Rock-paper-scissors suits
effect: A card may only be placed on another if its suit would not lose the matchup; ties resolve by higher rank.
note: An elemental cycle would be the natural flavour. It rewrites placement legality wholesale, so it is a rule card.

name: Effect-order deck section
effect: The deck view's top section lists every effect in firing order, hiding pips that do not affect whether the effect applies.
note: Question-mark pips collapse duplicates; the pip is revealed when only one card could be meant.

name: Suit variety combo
effect: Every distinct suit effect that fires adds to the combo, so a rainbow board beats a mono board on multiplier.
note: The anti-flush pressure that keeps four suits worth playing.

name: Negative ranks
effect: Ranks below zero, drawn under an inverting shader; props scoring a negative card subtract points but still add combo.
note: Trades points for multiplier, which is a real decision rather than a strict downside.

name: Stacking is a pip rule
effect: Stacking legality is decided by the topmost held card's own suit rule, the same way scoring cascade is decided by the scored card.
note: Shipped. It is what lets a single exotic suit carry its own placement rules.

name: Pick up from anywhere
effect: Consider dropping pickup rules entirely, since exotic suits make a general pickup rule hard to state.
note: Open question in the draft. The grid's answer is that placement is one-way unless an effect says otherwise.

name: Scoring grants spotlight
effect: Cards being scored are automatically in the spotlight as the score passes over them.
note: Shipped as the section's card list being the spotlight set. Scoring rules cards are live while their hand resolves.

name: Card art outlines
effect: Card art needs outlines because the card background colour is set by type and is not predictable.
note: A hard art constraint, not a preference.

name: Randomised scoring card
effect: A rule card that changes which melds are legal each show, American-mahjong style.
note: The single best replayability lever the rule deck offers, and a natural blind.

name: Trending talents
effect: Each show names talents or abilities that score extra, changing what a deck wants that night.
note: Same idea pointed at cards rather than melds. Pairs with the tastes-of-the-town blinds.

name: Game inspirations index
effect: The card-game survey that follows is the mining ground for melds, restrictions and blind objectives.
note: Every game below yields at least one mechanic; that is what the survey is for.

name: Mahjong melds
effect: Classic mahjong hands as an extension of the poker vocabulary - small straights of three, triplets and pairs.
note: Fits the five-card line better than fourteen-tile hands do.

name: Dragon suits
effect: Non-standard suits stand in for dragons, which implies more than three ranked suits and more than three dragons.
note: Winds are rejected in the draft as too directional - though the grid now has directions, so they are worth revisiting.

name: Mini hands
effect: A hand is one triplet plus a pair, scaling upward with each extra triplet, rather than a full fourteen-tile hand.
note: Sized to a five-card line. Four triplets and a pair is a whole-grid objective instead.

name: Unsorted melds
effect: Mahjong-style melds do not require the cards to be in order within the line.
note: Distinguishes them from runs, which do. A useful second axis for line design.

name: Mahjong discard
effect: Discard any card in a grid that belongs to no meld - a card with no connection to anything in its column.
note: The half-the-fun-is-discarding note, made spatial. Only fires on genuinely dead cards.

name: Themed meld rotation
effect: Each run names a few themed melds that score extra, so a different strategy is favoured each time.
note: Same shape as trending talents, aimed at melds. Both belong in the rule deck.

name: Cloud swirl shader
effect: Swirling cloud shaders as reference for the map's weather and the wall's backdrops.
note: Reference. Clouds can double as a picture frame on the map.

name: Gaussian glow with grain
effect: Colour-shifted Gaussian glow with grain, as reference for the lighting treatment.
note: Reference. Pairs with the blending-mode glow entry.

name: Cork-board map UI
effect: The map reads as a pinned cork board, but the pins are circus posters.
note: Diegetic and it makes route planning feel like planning.

name: Frame-reveal transitions
effect: Zooming out reveals the full frame around the image; transitions pan between differently framed images and zoom back in.
note: Shipped in shape by the picture wall. Undo reuses the same motion in reverse.

name: Confetti cone
effect: Confetti fired in a cone, with long streamers dropping from above.
note: The score celebration; scale it with the size of the score.

name: Diegetic UI wall
effect: All UI is one 2D space the camera pans around, like looking at a wall of framed photographs; the hub is a museum.
note: Shipped as the picture wall. The wide grid board is exactly what its saved pan exists for.

name: Framed start screen
effect: The start screen is itself a framed picture that zooms out when a tent is chosen; three tents are offered.
note: Three tents is the run-start choice - deck, difficulty and route in one gesture.

name: Living photographs
effect: Framed images on the wall are animated, not static.
note: Cheap life for a static hub.

name: Floating info cards
effect: In info mode, descriptions appear as floating notecards along the bottom of the screen.
note: Keeps explanation off the board, which matters on a board this wide.

name: Info card history
effect: Each info card opened goes into its own tab, so several can be compared side by side.
note: The right answer for a game where a combo spans four cards' text.

name: Back-tween motion
effect: Every motion overshoots slightly and anticipates before it starts.
note: Shipped in the grid's growth ease and spring.

name: Mult is one per effect
effect: The multiplier is simply plus one per distinct effect activated.
note: Shipped. The simplicity is the feature - every card visibly matters.

name: Clockwork theme
effect: Robert-Houdin's impossible clockwork machines as a design register for automata cards.
note: The Roman-numeral rank and the time-advancing effects belong to this family.

name: Mystery Clock
effect: A card with no visible mechanism that nonetheless announces when the next scoring line will complete.
note: Robert-Houdin's glass clock. Information as a card, which the game has too little of.

name: Singing Lesson
effect: Teaches an adjacent card one of its own triggers for the rest of the show.
note: Copying a trigger rather than an effect keeps it from being a strict upgrade.

name: Marvelous Orange Tree
effect: Grows over successive refills - budding, flowering, then fruiting a card into its own column.
note: Robert-Houdin's masterpiece. A card that pays out only if you protect its column for the whole show.

name: Pastrycook of Palais-Royal
effect: Cue to order a card by name from the discard; it is delivered to the Entrance next refill.
note: The automaton that fetched pastries on request. Targeted recursion with a delay.

name: Ethereal Suspension
effect: The card above this one floats - it neither blocks the spotlight nor counts toward stack height.
note: Robert-Houdin's levitation, and a direct counter to the cost of building tall.

name: The Bullet Catch
effect: Scores ten times its rank while spotlit, with a one-in-thirteen chance of destroying itself instead.
note: The trick that killed Chung Ling Soo. The purest near-miss in the design.

name: Endless Bag
effect: Cue to pull a random basic card out of nowhere into the Entrance; never runs out.
note: Infinite chaff is a real resource in a game where placement is the constraint.

name: Eating Contest
effect: Consumes every card in its own stack at show end and scores their combined rank.
note: A stack-capper that pays for building tall and then dismantles it.

name: Dog of 113 Tricks
effect: Each time a distinct effect fires anywhere this show, this card gains a permanent point, up to 113.
note: Rewards a rainbow board over a whole run rather than a whole line.

name: Free Pigs
effect: Gives a random card away to the audience - remove it from the deck and gain two tokens.
note: Barnum's giveaways. A thinning effect that pays instead of costing.

name: Ventriloquist
effect: An adjacent card's skill triggers as though it were this card's, from this card's position.
note: Relocating a trigger is a placement puzzle disguised as a copy effect.

name: Spirit Medium
effect: Cards stack themselves - at each refill, one loose card moves to a legal stack on its own.
note: Auto-moving cards give the board a life of its own, which is unnerving in the right way.

name: Teleport Boxes
effect: Cue to swap the contents of two cells, in any grids.
note: The cross-grid swap. Its whole value comes from there being more than one grid.

name: Levitation
