effect: Cue to raise this card one height level, leaving a gap beneath it that the next placement fills.
note: A verb only the fourth coordinate could support.

name: Narrative acts
effect: Presentation framed as plays and stories rather than as isolated tricks.
note: The scaffolding for quest-shaped effects that must fire in order.

name: Fake props
effect: A set-piece card that looks like a real card until it is scored, then reveals itself as worthless.
note: The Gaff. Its value is entirely in what an opponent or a blind believes about it.

name: Illusion film
effect: Melies-style combination of illusion and narrative as the register for the game's own presentation.
note: The film-grain transitions belong to this idea.

name: Golden Witch
effect: Spawns Gold cards onto the board through the show; every one of them detonates at show end.
note: Free money with a timer - the board fills with wealth you must spend before it goes off.

name: Narrative cards
effect: Protagonist and villain cards that play out a story across the board, scoring when their scenes complete in order.
note: The quest-shaped effect. Expensive to author, memorable when it lands.

name: The Dead List
effect: A separate collection for cards removed from play entirely, distinct from the discard, with its own board.
note: Naming it gives removal effects somewhere to point and a card family somewhere to fish from.

name: Poltergeist
effect: Vanishes an object - removes a card's suit, or repaints it to another suit already on the board.
note: The colour-changing half is the useful half; the vanishing half is the Clown class's job.

name: Crystal Ball
effect: Reveals the next several cards of the deck, as though the answers had been researched in advance.
note: The mitt-camp research gag makes the information feel earned rather than magical.

name: Self-Help Books
effect: Sell copies between shows - gain tokens scaled to how much fame the last show earned.
note: Turns a good show into money without touching the score axis.

name: Snake Charmer
effect: Cards in this column drift one cell toward this card at each refill.
note: Slow gravity, which lets a player set up a formation over several refills.

name: Tax Evasion
effect: Hold too many cards and the authorities take a cut of the deck; bribery and blackmail are the alternatives offered.
note: The consequence event for hoarding, and the counterweight to cards-as-currency.

name: Disappearing Birdcage
effect: Cue to remove this card and a neighbour from the board, returning both to the deck.
note: A reset button for a bad placement, which the one-way grid badly needs.

name: The Vanishing Chair
effect: At the end of each refill this card vanishes and reappears in a different empty cell of its grid.
note: Unpredictable but grid-local, so it never leaves the plan you built it into.

name: Multiplying Balls
effect: When a Balls card scores in this column, add a copy of it to the Entrance.
note: The suit-specific engine card, and the reason to commit a grid to one suit.

name: Expanding Dice
effect: Grows a rank each time a line containing it scores, without limit.
note: Simple, visible growth. The cap is how long you can protect the cell.

name: Nested Boxes
effect: Scores once for each card beneath it in its stack, each time multiplying rather than adding.
note: The card that most rewards a tall stack, and therefore the one that most needs a cost.

name: Self-Playing Instrument
effect: Triggers itself once per refill without being cued.
note: Automation as a card. It makes charges accumulate rather than expire.

name: Floating Head
effect: This card's skill detaches and floats over its grid, staying spotlit wherever it is buried.
note: The theatrical version of the always-active stamp, with the art to justify it.

name: The Band
effect: Scores extra for every distinct class present in its own line.
note: The rainbow reward at line scale rather than board scale.

name: Velocipede
effect: Cue to roll this card along its row until it hits an occupied cell, scoring each empty cell it crosses.
note: Movement that pays for empty space, which nothing else does.

name: Human Cannonball
effect: Cue to fire the bottom card of any stack into another grid's matching cell.
note: Reaches the unreachable card - the solitaire fantasy - and crosses grids doing it.

name: Vaudeville reference
effect: The vaudeville bill as a structure - seven to ten unrelated acts ordered to open safe, calm the middle and finish enormous.
note: Reference for pacing a show and for how a run's nodes should be ordered.

name: The Bill
effect: A show is ordered like a vaudeville bill - a silent opener that survives latecomers, novelty in the middle, the star second from last, and a closer that clears the room.
note: A pacing template for node ordering within a city.

name: Noah's Ark Box
effect: Cue to pour out a flood of animal-class cards into the deck, one per Animal Trainer card already owned.
note: Scales with commitment, which is the right shape for a legendary payoff.

name: Flower Cards
effect: Cards cut into flower shapes as a cosmetic card back or a pack variant.
note: Cosmetic only, but it is a strong pack identity.

name: Sleight of Hand
effect: Cards moved by effects sometimes land one cell off on purpose, and this card profits when they do.
note: Deliberate imprecision as a mechanic - risky, funny, and only viable with an undo.

name: Bricks from Hats
effect: Cue to convert this card's stamp into a token card placed in an empty cell.
note: Turns equipment back into material, which gives stamps a floor value.

name: Roast to Live Chicken
effect: Cue to bring one card back from the discard as a fresh copy at full rank.
note: Recursion with a transformation attached so it never feels like a plain undo.

name: Blindfold Knife Throw
effect: Cue to name a rank; a knife destroys one random card in the row and scores hugely if it was that rank.
note: Called-shot gambling. The showmanship is in naming it out loud before the throw.

name: The Shuffle
effect: Flips every card in a grid face down, randomises their positions, then reveals the topmost of each stack.
note: Total spatial reset. Terrifying, occasionally exactly what a stuck board needs.

name: Planted Props
effect: Cue to plant a card at a chosen depth in the draw deck, to be produced at exactly the right moment.
note: Prepping hours in advance is the actual trick; the card is just bookkeeping for it.

name: Fake Book Cover
effect: This card displays another card's name and art until it scores.
note: Misdirection as a stamp, and the mechanical partner of the Gaff.

name: Linking Rings
effect: Cards of the Hoops suit in the same row across separate grids count as one continuous line.
note: The long-row rule as a card. Directly rewards playing several grids at once.

name: Straitjacket over Spikes
effect: Starts immobilised over a hazard; frees itself and pays double if its line scores before the show ends.
note: The escape is the payoff. A self-solving problem with a deadline.

name: Niagara Crate
effect: Cue to seal this card and everything above it; the stack is out of play until the next refill, then returns intact.
note: Protects a built stack from a hazard at the cost of a refill's scoring.

name: Tornado of Fire
effect: Cue to set a column alight - every card in it gains Burning, and any card placed there this show gains it too.
note: Turns a column into a commitment. Pairs with anything that pays for Burning.

name: Escapology suite
effect: Jails, crates, safes, chains and manacles as the vocabulary for the Escape Artist class's restraint cards.
note: Each restraint is a different immobilisation with a different release condition.

name: Prince of the Air
effect: Leader whose cards may always move upward through a stack regardless of stacking rules.
note: The Acrobat leader. Height is its whole identity.

name: King of Cards
effect: Leader who may look at and reorder the top of the deck every refill.
note: The Fortune Teller leader. Information rather than power.

name: Lockpicking
effect: Cue to free any one immobilised or restricted card, including one restricted by a blind.
note: The counterplay card blinds need to exist for. Without it, restriction blinds are pure tax.

name: Buried Alive
effect: Scores enormously if it is buried under three or more cards when the show ends, and nothing otherwise.
note: Inverts every instinct the spotlight system trains. A deliberate contrarian card.

name: Timed Consumption
effect: Removing a card from play for a fixed number of refills, after which it returns, rather than removing it forever.
note: The mechanic behind Milk Can and the crate. Removal with a return is a tempo tool, not a loss.

name: Metamorphosis
effect: Cue to swap this card with any card in the draw deck, seen or unseen.
note: Houdini and Bess's substitution trunk. A controlled gamble with a body.

name: Vanishing Elephant
effect: Cue to remove the entire contents of one cell's stack from play; score for every card removed.
note: The largest single removal in the game, which is exactly what makes it a headline act.

name: Water Torture Cell
effect: Cue to start a three-refill timer; if this card's line has not scored by then, it is destroyed - if it has, it scores triple.
note: A deadline the player sets themselves. Tension without randomness.

name: Walking Through Walls
effect: This card may be placed into an occupied cell, pushing its occupant into the neighbouring grid's matching cell.
note: The clearest cross-grid verb, and it needs the row alignment rule to be legible at all.

name: Rising Cards
effect: Named cards rise out of the deck on their own and arrive in the Entrance at the next refill.
note: The classic effect, and a clean tutor.

name: Disembodied Princess
effect: Only the top half of this card is ever covered - it stays spotlit no matter how tall its stack grows.
note: The illusion and the mechanic are the same picture, which is the ideal for this game.

name: Floating Ball
effect: Cue to send a hoop prop around a Balls card to prove it is unsupported, scoring both.
note: A two-suit combo card that reads as an actual trick.

name: Fake Blood
effect: Appears to destroy an adjacent card; it is only hidden and returns next refill, scoring for the fright.
note: Payoff for the audience believing something went wrong - the risk essay in one card.

name: Indian Rope Trick
effect: Cue to raise a column of cards into a new stack in a single cell, climbing them all upward.
note: Converts spread into height, which is a whole strategy pivot in one action.

name: Tire Trick
effect: Cue to dismantle a stack, hiding its cards; rebuilding the stack later returns them all.
note: Storage that reads as a trick. Pairs with any hazard that targets a stack.

name: Everlasting Flame
effect: Burning applied by this card is not removed by anything, including effects that clear statuses.
note: The counter to status removal, and a reason to keep a Flames build honest.

name: Human Card Index
effect: Cue to name any rank and suit; if that card exists anywhere in your collections, it arrives in the Entrance.
note: The perfect tutor, and the historical act is exactly this - over forty pockets and hundreds of items.

name: Bullfight
effect: A charging prop crosses the row; cards that dodge score, cards that do not are destroyed.
note: A prop that can lose you cards is the risk-reward shape hazards should have.

name: The Sawing
effect: Cue to split a card into two cards of half its rank, same suit, placed in adjacent cells.
note: Rank arithmetic as a tool - fabricate a run on demand.

name: The Expert at the Card Table
effect: Signed by an author nobody can identify; collecting every card bearing the signature unlocks something never explained.
note: The Erdnase cipher. One field on a card, and the community does the rest.

name: Signed Card
effect: When this card leaves the board, the next card created anywhere is this exact card instead.
note: Identity that survives destruction, which no other effect provides.

name: Misdirection
effect: While spotlit, the lowest covered card in each adjacent column is also spotlit.
note: A spatial aura - one placement relights a whole region of the board.

name: Cups and Balls
effect: Cue to shuffle the positions of three adjacent face-down cards.
note: The oldest trick recorded, and a fine cheap tutorial for the hidden-card rules.

name: Collection names
effect: The collections are named - the Dead List for removed cards with its own board, Backstage, the Grand Entrance, the Ring, and the Magic Deck for rules.
note: Vocabulary that the code partly adopted; the Dead List is still unbuilt.

name: Rest Area
effect: A named between-shows collection where cards recover from statuses and exhaustion.
note: Gives rest-based costs like Maximum Effort somewhere to point.

name: Mentalist
effect: Cue to predict a future board state; if it comes true this show, score enormously.
note: Rewards reading the deck and the grid together, which nothing else asks for.

name: Magic musicals
effect: Magic staged as a musical number rather than as a trick, as a presentation register.
note: Supports the effect-art pop-up idea - a fired effect is a number, not a notification.

name: Turning Back Time
effect: Cue to undo the last placement without spending an undo, framed as covering an accident.
note: Undo as a card is powerful precisely because the grid commits placements.

name: Ground acrobatics
effect: Hand-walking, cartwheels, contortion, splits and somersaults as the Acrobat class's art vocabulary.
note: Art reference for a class whose cards are all movement verbs.

name: Arena spectacle
effect: Chariot races, gladiators, animal baiting - the Roman ancestor of the ring, and the source of the word circus.
note: The oldest layer of the theme, and the reason Roman numerals are a rank skin.

name: Medieval troupe
effect: Tumblers, dancers, musicians, jesters, caravans and aerialists travelling together as one company.
note: The troupe-as-deck framing, sourced.

name: Funambulist
effect: Crosses its row one cell per refill; if it reaches the far end it scores hugely, and any disturbance drops it.
note: Rope walking as a multi-turn commitment the opponent - or a blind - can interrupt.

name: Slack Rope
effect: This card may be placed between two occupied cells, shifting both outward.
note: Mountebanks walked slack ropes. An insertion verb, which the grid otherwise lacks.

name: Hubris
effect: A card that has scored hugely gains Hubris and risks a penalty on its next score.
note: The bad-luck-for-hubris tradition, and a soft cap on repeat scoring.

name: Endurance feats
effect: Coal walking, boiling oil, fire swallowing - cards that score for surviving a hazard they were placed into deliberately.
note: The template for any card that wants a blind to exist.

name: Animal novelty
effect: Upright dogs, costumed monkeys, dancing turkeys - low-rarity Animal Trainer cards that score for adjacency to their trainer.
note: The common tier of a class needs cheap adjacency cards like these.

name: Costumed Acrobat
effect: An Acrobat dressed as a beast counts as an Animal card as well as an Acrobat.
note: Class splashing with a historical excuse. The Greasepaint stamp generalises it.

name: Trained Bear
effect: Eats the card directly above it at each refill and gains its rank.
note: Height gives the bear a queue to work through, which paces it naturally.

name: Puppet
effect: Copies the skill of the card to its left for as long as that card remains in play.
note: Puppetry as a copy effect with a visible string - the dependency is the drama.

name: Potion Seller
effect: Cue to sell a card from the deck for tokens; the buyer is never seen again.
note: Saltimbanque economics. A thinning outlet inside a show rather than at a shop.

name: Pickpocket
effect: If this card ends the show without ever scoring, it adds a stolen card to the deck.
note: Rewards not playing a card, which almost nothing else does.

name: Commedia playlet
effect: Short pantomimes and playlets predate clowning and are its source; commedia dell'arte is the ancestor.
note: Sourcing for the Clown class and for the narrative-cards idea.

name: Head in the Lion's Mouth
effect: Place adjacent to an Animal card to score triple; if that Animal is ever destroyed, this card is too.
note: Risk stated as a dependency rather than as a dice roll.

name: National styles
effect: French trapeze, German Icarian games, Anglo-Saxon horseback, Spanish lightness, Japanese balancing, Arab fire - the historical specialisms.
note: A ready-made way to give card families visual and mechanical identity.

name: Diversity as combo
effect: Circus managers sold the world in one tent; the game's equivalent is that variety on the board scores better than sameness.
note: The framing that makes the anti-flush pressure thematic rather than arbitrary. Handle the historical framing carefully.

name: Troupe insularity
effect: Performers kept to themselves and did not mingle with the towns they played.
note: Flavour for the union-strike and consequence events.

name: The Ring is Freedom
effect: The ring has neither beginning nor end - the line worth putting on the title screen.
note: Flavour. It also happens to describe a grid with wrapping movement.

name: Running away to the circus
effect: The dream of glamour, adventure and escape that the game's fiction sells.
note: The run's implicit premise; worth one line of framing at run start.

name: Injury stacks
effect: Each trigger risks an injury stack; enough stacks retire the card permanently. Sitting out a show clears one.
note: The real history of the no-net era. It makes over-triggering a card a genuine cost.

name: Applause curve
effect: Applause scales with the score, with individual gasps for individual high-scoring cards.
note: The audience-as-antagonist made audible. Cheap and enormously effective.

name: Military Riders
effect: Scores extra when in a row with two or more cards of its own class, standing in formation.
note: The plainest class-count card, and the tutorial for the autochess rule.

name: Playing Dead
effect: This card is skipped by every destructive effect while it is face down.
note: Protection that costs the card its own scoring while it hides.

name: Canvas cover
effect: Rain stops the show unless the tent is covered - a weather blind that disables scoring until a condition is met.
note: A blind with an on-switch rather than a permanent tax.

name: Automaton and magnet
effect: Cue to pull the nearest card of a chosen suit one cell toward this one.
note: Mechanical attraction as a targeted move, with the magnet as the honest explanation.

name: Long Hair
effect: Hangs from the card above it - counts as part of the stack above rather than below when a line is read.
note: Iron-jaw-by-hair, and a genuinely odd geometry effect.

name: Ring and stage
effect: A full ring at the centre and a theatre stage at the side, for combination spectacles.
note: The historical precedent for several performance spaces at once - which is the multi-grid board.

name: Leaping the Horse
effect: Cue to jump this card back and forth over a neighbour, scoring once per crossing, until it fails.
note: Forty crossings without stopping is the record; the card should tempt the player to push one more.

name: Standing Split
effect: Scores double while it is the only card in its column, and nothing at all once it is not.
note: A card that wants an empty column, which fights every other incentive.

name: The Whip
effect: Performers and animals are driven harder - every card triggers an extra time, and every card gains an injury stack.
note: Upside and downside in the same clause, which is the shape every blind should have.

name: Eight-Horse Platform
effect: Scores once per card in its row that is directly supporting it - every card below in the same column counts.
note: Reads the board in two axes at once, which is the grid's signature shape.

name: Catching Oranges
effect: Cue to catch the next prop that would pass this card, scoring it instead of letting it continue.
note: Prop interception - a defensive verb in a system that had only offence.

name: Juggling Variety
effect: Scores once per distinct object type juggled in its column - fruit, bottles, glasses, hoops.
note: A per-column variety reward to sit beside the per-line one.

name: Human Pyramid
effect: Scores for a stack whose ranks strictly decrease upward, once per card in the stack.
note: The formation card the fourth coordinate exists for.

name: Shipwreck Spectacle
effect: Grand staged productions - shipwrecks and battles - as large event nodes with their own boards.
note: The set-piece node type, distinct from a shop or a fight.

name: The Infirmary
effect: A between-shows space that clears injury and exhaustion from cards left there.
note: Amphitheatres doubled as hospitals. Gives the injury system an off-ramp.

name: Hippodrama
effect: Animal cards may take the leading role - while this is in play, Animal cards count as performers for every class check.
note: Horses treated as actors with billing. A class-wide unlock in one card.

name: The Drunk Spectator
effect: Enters as an ordinary basic card and reveals itself as a performer after it has scored once.
note: The oldest gag in the ring, and a genuinely good surprise the second time you see it.

name: Ordered quests
effect: Some effects require a sequence - the next stage unlocks only when the previous one has fired.
note: The quest-shaped effect. It is also exactly how a multi-part blind objective should read.

name: Costume appeal
effect: Skin-coloured bodysuits, cross-dressed performers and dominatrix framing all sold tickets historically.
note: Historical record. Handle with care in art direction; the reference file has the caveats.

name: Carried Talent
effect: A talent card stacked on another talent card scores extra, scaling with how many talents are beneath it.
note: Tricks performed atop other performers. The most direct height reward in the notes.

name: Water Ring
effect: The floor floods - the bottom row of every grid cannot be used until a diving card is placed.
note: A blind that removes space rather than points, and sells a specific card as its answer.

name: Iron Jaw
effect: Supports the entire stack above it - cards above cannot be destroyed or moved while this card holds.
note: Holding weight between the teeth. Anchors a tall stack against hazards.

name: One act at a time
effect: Three rings at once was too noisy; a single act allowed the audience to follow performers and their careers.
note: The argument for the focused single-grid view being the default over the zoomed-out one.

name: The Parade
effect: The troupe parades through the town while the tent goes up - the show's opening animation.
note: Free spectacle over an unavoidable load.

name: Why there are rings
effect: Extra rings existed to seat more people without putting anyone too far from an act; every seat has a nearest ring, but can still see the others.
note: The best possible justification for the multi-grid board and its two view modes.

name: Stuffed titles
effect: Circus names were absurd accretions of claims; generate them procedurally.
note: Free procedural flavour, and it makes each run's troupe feel named.

name: Four tents one ticket
effect: A city node contains several attractions - menagerie, museum, minstrels, main ring - visited on one ticket.
note: Turns a city into a small map of its own rather than a single encounter.

name: Troupe roles
effect: Manager, advertiser, treasurer, equestrian director, band leader, lion performer, elephant man, doorkeeper, ostler, grooms, tent men.
note: A ready-made name list for Producer-class cards.

name: Lion Act
effect: Lions form pedestals, seesaws and bicycles - scores for each distinct formation shape completed in its row.
note: A card that reads shapes, which the diagonal bucket makes possible.

name: Hippodrome Track
effect: A track outside the ring - a row beneath the grid that cards can race along without occupying cells.
note: The Entrance is already row -1; this is its mirror at the bottom, and a natural home for props.

name: Ringling Modesty
effect: A respectable town - flashy cards score nothing, and only common and uncommon cards pay.
note: The blind that punishes a deck of legendaries, which is the deck most players build.

name: Electric Light
effect: Generators allow night shows - a second show at the same node, with different rules.
note: Doubles a node's content for the cost of a palette swap.

name: Ballet of Elephants
effect: Scores for every Animal card in the grid that shares its row or column with a Dancer card.
note: Fifty ballerinas on fifty elephants. A whole-grid formation payoff.

name: Clown Fire House
effect: When a column burns, clown cards rush in - each Clown in the grid scores and clears one Burning stack.
note: The slapstick skit as counterplay to the game's own fire.

name: Mud Show
effect: An unpaved route - picking up any card costs a discard.
note: Taxes movement rather than scoring, which hits an entirely different deck.

name: Concessions vendors
effect: Peanut, candy, popcorn, balloon and lemonade sellers - common cards that pay tokens when adjacent cards score.
note: The common tier of the Concessions class, and the economy's trickle.

name: Flamboyant pseudonyms
effect: Equescurriculum, hippolymiad, cirqzooladon - invented grandiose words for the name generator.
note: Pure flavour, and the funnier for being real.

name: Jungle Cats
effect: Panthers and leopards - an Animal card that destroys an adjacent card if no Animal Trainer shares its line.
note: An animal that needs handling, which makes the trainer cards matter.

name: The Calliope
effect: Adds to the combo for every distinct class that scored this show.
note: Heard for miles before the circus arrived. The rainbow reward at show scale.

name: Flaming Cauldron
effect: Cue to dive this card down its whole column, destroying it and scoring for every Burning card it passes.
note: A finisher that spends the card and the column together.

name: Pyrotechnics
effect: Roman candles, rockets, pinwheels and coloured fire as the Fireworks suit's visual language.
note: Art direction for the suit that already ships.

name: Automaton Procession
effect: Mechanical gymnasts and trapezists parade across a row at each refill, triggering each card they pass.
note: A prop that walks the row on a schedule rather than on a score.

name: Limelight
effect: Limelight is the older word for spotlight, and calcium light lit the night parades.
note: Vocabulary with a source; worth using in the tutorial text.

name: Niagara Crossing
effect: Cue to walk this card across every grid in one move, scoring for each cell it crosses and falling if any is occupied.
note: A thousand feet of cable, and the longest single move the board allows.

name: Balance Pole
effect: The card this is attached to cannot fail a risk check.
note: The insurance stamp for every gamble card, and the thing a blind should be able to remove.

name: Trapeze Chain
effect: Requires a catcher and a returner - three cards in a row, each triggering the next, scoring more per link.
note: The trapeze act's real structure as a three-card combo.

name: The Net
effect: Cards in this grid cannot be destroyed, but every card scores less while it hangs.
note: Nets turned fear into awe, and audiences valued the act less. The mechanic says exactly that.

name: Balloon Craze
effect: Aerialist popularity rode the balloon craze - fashions in spectacle move together.
note: Justifies trending-talent rotation as a historical fact rather than a game-ism.

name: Deliberate Wobble
effect: Cue to fake a mistake - lose points now, and score triple if this card's line completes anyway.
note: The risk essay's thesis card. Performers wobbled on purpose because the gasp was the act.

name: The Web
effect: Dangling ropes - cue to hang a card from the top of its column down to the first empty cell.
note: Aerial ballet as a placement verb, and a use for empty cells low in a column.

name: The Plange
effect: Repeats its own trigger as many times as you dare; each repeat after the first risks an injury stack.
note: Leitzel's one-arm planges, which dislocated her shoulder every performance. Push-your-luck with a real cost.

name: The Triple
effect: Scores triple if it completes a run of exactly three assembled this refill, and blacks out - skipping its next trigger.
note: The salto mortale, including the blackout after the second turn.

name: The Low Wire
effect: Only seven feet up but twice as long - moves two cells along its row instead of one, but never changes height.
note: A cheap movement card that trades the fourth coordinate away for reach.

name: Forward Somersault
effect: Moves upward through its stack blind - the destination is not shown until the move resolves.
note: Harder than backwards because the wire cannot be seen. Risk from information, not dice.

name: Human Pyramid on the Wire
effect: Scores for a stack of seven or more, and collapses the whole stack if any card in it is removed.
note: Seven men on one wire. The largest formation payoff with the largest fragility.

name: Wire Bicycle
effect: Carries the card above it along the row as it moves.
note: Transporting a passenger is a distinct verb from moving alone.

name: The Fake Leg
effect: A card wearing this ignores one restriction placed on it by a blind.
note: Wire walking after an amputation. Counterplay stated as equipment.

name: Slipped Straps
effect: Cue to drop this card to the bottom of its stack, scoring for each card it falls past.
note: The faked free fall. A downward verb on a board that otherwise only builds upward.

name: Twenty Tigers
effect: Scores for every Animal card in the grid, and gives this card an injury stack for each one.
note: Wounds flaunted rather than hidden - the scar is the credential.

name: Menagerie
effect: Scores for each distinct Animal card you have ever owned this run.
note: The oddity collection as a long-run reward.

name: Elephants
effect: Only affordable to a wealthy troupe - costs upkeep in tokens every show it stays in the deck.
note: Historically true and mechanically sound: the best cards should cost rent.

name: Lion Pyramid
effect: Scores for a stack made entirely of Animal cards, scaling with its height.
note: The class-specific height formation.

name: Fake Blood Spectacle
effect: Appears to be destroyed when a hazard hits it; it returns at the next refill, and the fright scores.
note: The gorier the better, historically. A survivable destruction is more exciting than a real one.

name: Enraged Beast
effect: Grows more dangerous each refill until an Animal Trainer card is placed in its line, then scores everything it built.
note: Manufactured rage subdued by mastery - a threat that becomes a payoff.

name: Lamb in the Lion Cage
effect: A rank-1 card placed beside an Animal card cannot be destroyed, and both score.
note: Peace as the trick. A defensive card that pays.

name: Peaceful Menagerie
effect: If no card was destroyed this show, every Animal card scores double at the end.
note: The pacifist run condition, and a real strategic fork.

name: Animal Tricks
effect: Globes, tightropes, bicycles and seesaws - common Animal cards that each move one specific way.
note: The common tier of movement, one verb per card.

name: The Animal King
effect: Leader whose Animal cards never gain injury stacks and never turn on their trainer.
note: The Animal Trainer leader.

name: Wrestling the Tiger
effect: Cue to fight an adjacent Animal card - the higher rank wins, the loser is destroyed, the winner scores both ranks.
note: A duel inside a solitaire game, which is a genuinely novel verb.

name: Tarzan
effect: Swings across the row from Animal card to Animal card, scoring at each.
note: Movement that requires a prepared path, which makes the setup the play.

name: Concrete skill art
effect: Skill art must depict a real circus prop or performer, never an abstraction - a mahjong ruleset becomes a dragon, American mahjong an eagle.
note: Owner ruling, and the reason every card in this file carries a real referent.

name: Risk scales with reward
effect: Higher-tier tricks fail more often; risk-lowering cards are the counterplay, and doubling points is the opt-in.
note: The costing rule for the whole gamble family.

name: Clown entree
effect: Clowns get extended solo acts in the centre of the ring - a Clown card may take a whole refill for itself.
note: Gives the Clown class a structural privilege rather than a numeric one.

name: Soul of the circus
effect: Clowns are the soul of the circus and the most technically demanding role, not the simplest.
note: The argument for the Clown class being the rules-bending class rather than the joke class.

name: Three clown types
effect: Whiteface, Auguste and the grotesque - three clown archetypes with three different mechanical registers.
note: Three sub-families inside one class, which is enough identity for a whole set.

name: Commedia archetypes
effect: The innocent, the devious cheat, the buffoon, the yokel and the comic servant as clown prototypes.
note: Five named characters, five card personalities.

name: Satire and sympathy
effect: Commedia skits worked because the audience recognised themselves; laughing at the clown is laughing at yourself.
note: The tonal rule for clown card text - open about intent, vulnerable, never cruel.

name: Named clowns
effect: Grimaldi, Deburau, Harlequin, Merry Andrew and Pierrot as the historical roster.
note: Names with real biographies attached, which is free flavour text.

name: Little man in a confusing world
effect: The enduring clown theme, and the register the game's failure states should adopt.
note: Losing a show should feel like a Weary Willie bit, not a game-over.

name: Exaggerated makeup
effect: Clown makeup exists to project emotion across a large theatre - the same problem card art has at small size.
note: A historical argument for the game's own readability rules.

name: Colour-themed clowns
effect: Whiteface clowns keyed to colour - each changes a neighbour's suit to its own.
note: The Clown class's core verb, split across a colour-coded set.

name: Clown as any character
effect: A Clown card may count as any class for one check per refill, since clowns caricature everyone.
note: Class wildcarding with a strong historical justification.

name: Clown as the story
effect: The clown is the story he enacts - adoration, devotion, crucifixion.
note: Tone reference for the narrative cards.

name: Circular flow
effect: The circus as circular forms unrolling without pause - flow rather than reflection.
note: The argument for a show that never stops to ask the player to confirm anything.

name: Clown Parody
effect: Copies the effect of a card in the same row and scores half of what it scored.
note: Clowns spoofed the rope walkers and the riders. Copying is the class's other verb.

name: Speaking Clown
effect: Announces the next scoring line aloud, revealing what would complete it.
note: Information as banter. Cheap, and it teaches the game.

name: Auguste and Whiteface
effect: The Auguste scores when it fails; the Whiteface scores when it succeeds; together in a row both always score.
note: The defeated clown and the aspiring one, and a two-card engine that always fires.

name: Dan Rice
effect: Leader whose Clown cards may cue twice per refill, talking, singing and dancing through the show.
note: The Clown leader, and the historical superstar clown of American circus.

name: The Successful Clown
effect: A clown must be mimic, elocutionist and satirist - a fool to the ringmaster and a wise man to the audience.
note: The best available flavour text for the Clown leader card.

name: Slapstick
effect: Cue to swap the ranks of this card and one adjacent card.
note: The literal battacio of commedia. The cheapest and most useful pip fixer.

name: Grock
effect: Copies the last effect that triggered anywhere on the board, whatever it was.
note: The funniest clown in the world, and an infinitely mobile effect to match the face.

name: Weary Willie
effect: Gains a permanent rank every time one of your cards is destroyed or a show is failed.
note: Emmett Kelly's tramp. A loss-compensator that turns a bad run into a souvenir.

name: New Clowning
effect: Modern clowning aims to make the audience think rather than laugh, seeking connection over gags.
note: Justifies clown cards that do strange, quiet things rather than loud ones.

name: Transgressive Clown
effect: While in play, one rule card in the rule deck is suspended.
note: Jesters upset the rules of everyday life. The most dangerous card family in the game.

name: The Shortchanging Clown
effect: Pays out tokens now and takes more back at the end of the show.
note: Krusty, the clown who shortchanges the rube. A loan with a face.

name: Cannon Chain
effect: A card fired into a cell containing another cannon is fired again from there, chaining across grids.
note: Explicitly asked for in the newest draft; the cross-grid chain is the payoff.

name: The Great Fall
effect: Cue to drop this card from the top of its stack to the board, scoring for the height it fell.
note: Falling as an act in itself. The mirror of every upward verb.

name: Cannon Woman
effect: Cue to fire this card to the matching cell of an adjacent grid.
note: The clean single-hop cross-grid move, cheaper than the chain.

name: Hair Hang
effect: While hanging beneath another card, this card may still be cued, and scores for the cards above it.
note: Hanging by braided hair while juggling - an act performed from underneath.

name: Strongman Feats
effect: Supports any number of cards above it without the stack becoming unstable.
note: Granite on the torso. The enabler for very tall stacks.

name: Risley Act
effect: Juggles the cards above it - at each refill their order is reversed.
note: Foot juggling of people. Reordering a stack without dismantling it is a rare verb.

name: Juggling Objects
effect: Plates, hoops, knives, clubs, fruit and the famously impossible eggs - the prop vocabulary and its difficulty ladder.
note: Prop art reference, and a natural rarity ladder for prop cards.

name: Exotic Jugglers
effect: Japanese, Indian and Chinese jugglers dominated the discipline and were marketed as exotic.
note: Historical record; the reference file carries the framing caveats.

name: Sword Swallower
effect: Cue to swallow the card directly above it - removed from play, and this card scores its rank.
note: Consumption upward instead of downward, which the flip made possible.

name: India-Rubber Man
effect: May be placed in any cell regardless of any placement restriction.
note: Elastic and incomprehensible. The universal answer to restriction blinds.

name: Ladder Violinist
effect: Moves up and down its column each refill, triggering the card it lands on.
note: Two acts at once, which is the joke and the mechanic.

name: Human Corkscrew
effect: Cue to move this card through an occupied cell to the empty cell beyond it.
note: Going through the keyhole. Passing through occupation is a genuinely new movement rule.

name: Prodigies
effect: The sideshow performers - conjoined, limbless, hirsute, tiny, tall - called prodigies rather than freaks.
note: The Freakshow class's roster. The reference file's handle-with-care section governs the treatment.

name: Sideshow bill
effect: The full historical bill - snake trainer, giants, comedy jugglers, sword swallower, tattooed strongman, magician, rubber-armed man, living skeleton, midget musician, human dynamo.
note: A complete named roster for one card set.

name: Fun House Mirror
effect: Distorts adjacent effects - each neighbour's effect fires at double or half strength, chosen at placement.
note: The meta-effect card that the draft itself proposes in the same line.

name: Human Cigarette Factory
effect: Produces one token card per refill using nothing but itself.
note: A self-sufficient generator, priced low because tokens are cheap.

name: Roller Skating
effect: Cue to slide this card one cell along its row into an empty cell.
note: The cheapest movement card in the game, and the one that teaches the verb.

name: Contemporary register
effect: Rock and roll in the modern circus - the historical material need not sound historical.
note: Licence for the soundtrack to be contemporary while the art is not.

name: Injury and retirement
effect: Each trigger risks injury; injury stacks raise the chance of permanent retirement; a show spent idle clears one stack.
note: The full loop, stated once. The Net raises injury and lowers retirement, which is exactly what nets did.

name: Critical hits
effect: Scores can crit, multiplying a single line's payout.
note: Variance on the upside to match injury's variance on the downside.

name: Five base suits
effect: Five suits rather than four - flushes get harder and an anti-flush hand becomes possible.
note: Directly contradicts the recommendations' four-suit argument. Owner's call, and the newer line.

name: Solitaire vocabulary
effect: Layout, tableau, pile, building, legal move, foundation, space, stock, waste, redeal, merci - the standard terms.
note: The shared language the design docs should use for anything solitaire-shaped.

name: Merci
effect: One free illegal move per show, from the solitaire tradition of a single permitted cheat.
note: A named, historical, once-per-show escape hatch. Perfect as a starting-deck card.

name: Accordion combining
effect: Cards three apart in a row, or directly adjacent, may be merged if they match by rank or suit.
note: Accordion solitaire's whole game, as one card. The three-apart rule is the interesting half.

name: Calculation counting
effect: Columns score for arithmetic sequences - ones, twos, threes and fours, wrapping around the rank range.
note: Calculation solitaire's foundations. A completely different column reading to runs.

name: Reserve pile
effect: A face-up reserve of cards outside the grid that may be played to any legal cell.
note: Canfield's demon. A second Entrance with different rules, and a real strategic resource.

name: Foundation building
effect: Four foundation cells that must be built up in suit from a base rank set at show start.
note: Canfield and Klondike's shared goal, offered as an alternate win condition.

name: Klondike layout
effect: Seven columns of increasing depth with only the top card visible.
note: An alternate grid shape for an event or a puzzle level.

name: Fan layout
effect: Seventeen small piles of three cards plus one single - only top cards are playable, with three redeals.
note: La Belle Lucie. A wide shallow board, the opposite of the tall grid.

name: Poker Squares
effect: Twenty-five cards in a five-by-five square make ten poker hands from five rows and five columns.
note: The core the whole overhaul is named for. Shipped.

name: Adjacency placement
effect: Each card must be placed adjacent or diagonal to one already placed, so the first card can end up anywhere.
note: Not the default here, but exactly the newest draft's boss-entrance restriction.

name: Flushes are easy here
effect: Flushes are rare in poker but common in poker patience, which is why the payout table differs.
note: The reason the game uses Barry scoring rather than poker odds.

name: Barry scoring target
effect: Two hundred points across all rows and columns is the traditional win in Barry scoring.
note: The historical benchmark the goal curve should be sanity-checked against.

name: Long diagonals
effect: The two long diagonals score as an optional variation.
note: Adopted, and extended - every diagonal family banks into the one special bucket.

name: Same-cards PvP
effect: Both players build their own square from the same cards in the same order.
note: Free PvP from a deterministic deck; the grid makes it trivially implementable.

name: Poker payout table
effect: The UK and Barry payout tables for each hand, from pair through straight flush.
note: The two reference tables the economy should be tuned against.

name: Two Pair payout
effect: Two pair pays 3 under UK scoring and 5 under Barry.
note: Reference row of the payout table.

name: Three of a kind payout
effect: Three of a kind pays 6 under UK scoring and 10 under Barry.
note: Reference row of the payout table.

name: Straight payout
effect: A straight pays 12 under UK scoring and 25 under Barry - Barry rates straights above flushes, unlike poker.
note: The single most important row: Barry scoring is tuned for the grid's odds, not poker's.

name: Flush payout
effect: A flush pays 5 under UK scoring and 15 under Barry, well below a straight.
note: Because flushes are easy on a grid you build yourself.

name: Full House payout
effect: A full house pays 10 under UK scoring and 50 under Barry.
note: Reference row of the payout table.

name: Four of a Kind payout
effect: Four of a kind pays 16 under UK scoring and 70 under Barry.
note: Reference row of the payout table.

name: Straight Flush payout
effect: A straight or royal flush pays 30 under UK scoring and 100 under Barry.
note: The ceiling the game's own top hand should be measured against.

name: Poker Patience replaces the tableau
effect: The Entrance keeps its five cards, but the player chooses where each one goes in a five-by-five grid below.
note: The decision that produced this whole document. Shipped.

name: Three grids
effect: A show fills several grids side by side; effects can reach across them, and committing to one grid commits the whole Entrance to it.
note: Shipped. Free grid-hopping is rejected because a fixed deck would let you replay the same placements.

name: Long rows across grids
effect: A row may be read as one continuous line across every open grid.
note: The reason cross-grid row alignment had to be exact, and why it has its own setting.

name: Order matters
effect: The format shifts the game's difficulty from stack management to the order cards are placed in, Noita-style.
note: The honest description of what the overhaul changed about play.

name: Cross-grid bounce
effect: Effects that throw a card into another grid, or swap two cards between grids.
note: The card family the third coordinate exists to serve.

name: Placement freedom
effect: Cards may be placed in any empty cell with no adjacency requirement.
note: Shipped as the default. The adjacency variant survives as a blind.

name: Grids per deck size
effect: Every twenty-five cards of deck unlocks another grid, capped so a huge deck does not become unmanageable.
note: Shipped as SkillGridAllotment. A deck the same size as one grid would let you place perfectly, so the ratio matters.

name: Stacking on a full grid
effect: Cards may be stacked on placed cards, adding rows and columns above the flat grid.
note: Shipped. It is the answer to every card being visible from the start.

name: Grid-local or global
effect: Every effect declares whether it acts within its own grid or across the whole board.
note: The axis this entire file is sorted by, and the owner's standing instruction for new effects.

name: Cross-grid triggers
effect: Whether an effect in one grid may fire while the player is placing in another.
note: Open. Global effects say yes by definition; grid-local ones say no.

name: Reuse the zone architecture
effect: A five-by-five grid is five stacked zones, each allowing stacking, reusing the existing covering mechanic.
note: The insight that made the overhaul affordable. High card stays because rank is not always ordinary.

name: Alternative grid layouts
effect: Grids need not be five by five, and cells may be pre-filled with cards or hazards.
note: The mechanical basis for most of the blinds category.

name: Score on completion
effect: A line scores the instant it completes rather than at the end of the show.
note: Shipped. Cards may still hook the completion event to reward finishing early or late.

name: Triggers stay the multiplier
effect: Effect triggers continue to supply the multiplier.
note: Unchanged by the overhaul, which is why the economy survived it.

name: Built-in PvP
effect: Two players start with the same deck and race for the higher score.
note: Nearly free once the deck is deterministic and placement is the only decision.

name: Unused entrance cards persist
effect: Cards left in the Entrance stay there and are not replaced until the whole Entrance empties.
note: Shipped. It is what makes holding a card for later a real option.

name: AI feasibility
effect: Fixed cells make the game far easier to write an AI for than a stack-dependent tableau.
note: Useful for balance simulation long before it is useful for an opponent.

name: Whole-grid mahjong hands
effect: A grid scores if its five rows, or its five columns, contain four triplets and a pair between them.
note: A meld read across a grid rather than a line - the special bucket's natural home.

name: Mancala cells
effect: An empty cell can be given a rule of its own - it raises or lowers the rank of whatever is placed there, showing the modifier before you commit.
note: The single most reusable blind mechanic, and it is already visible in the cell.

name: Poker squares reference
effect: The Wikipedia entry for poker squares, the game's direct ancestor.
note: Reference.

name: Poker Shuffle
effect: Cue to rearrange any cards already placed, before the grid is full.
note: Explicitly game-breaking - it makes a perfect grid inevitable. Print it once, price it as a legendary.

name: Communal foundation
effect: A shared foundation both players build into, ace through queen, king wild, four at a time.
note: Spite and Malice's core. The natural shape for a co-op or versus mode.

name: Personal waste pile
effect: A personal discard that may only be stacked downward or level, whose top card is playable.
note: A discard with rules is a resource; a discard without them is a bin.

name: Forfeit ranks
effect: Face cards demand a forfeit from the next card placed - four cards for an ace, three for a king, two for a queen, one for a jack.
note: Beggar My Neighbor's escalation, and a fine blind: face cards tax the next placement.

name: Snap match
effect: When a card is placed matching the rank of the last card placed, both score.
note: Snap, Slapjack and War in one line - reward for consecutive placements matching.

name: Go Fish tutor
effect: Cue to name a rank you already hold; every copy of it in the deck comes to the Entrance.
note: Go Fish's ask, and the requirement to already hold one keeps it honest.

name: Bluffed cards
effect: Cards may be placed face down claiming to be something else; an effect can call the bluff and punish a lie.
note: Cheat, as a mechanic. Only meaningful with an opponent or a suspicious blind.

name: Old Maid
effect: A card that cannot be discarded normally and penalises you for holding it at show end; pairs it off to be rid of it.
note: A hot-potato card, which the deck economy currently has no example of.

name: Speed stacking
effect: A no-turn-order mode where both players place simultaneously onto shared cells.
note: Spit. A real-time variant the grid could host without new rules.

name: Rummy melds
effect: Three of a suit in sequence, or three to four of a rank, as an alternative meld vocabulary.
note: Close enough to poker to be swappable, different enough to change what a deck wants.

name: Laying off
effect: Score a partial meld early to bank it, at the risk that another card completes it for someone else's benefit.
note: The bank-now-or-build decision, which the immediate-scoring grid already half-implements.

name: Wild card designation
effect: A named rank is wild for the whole show.
note: Rummy's option and Canasta's twos. A trivially good blind or event reward.

name: Going out early
effect: Declare the show over while ahead and take a bonus for finishing with the board incomplete.
note: Gin Rummy's knock. It gives the End button a reason to be pressed early.

name: Steal a meld
effect: Cue to add a card to a line that has already scored, rescoring the whole line.
note: 500 Rummy's out-of-turn steal. Rescoring is the strongest verb in the game, so charge for it.

name: Wild stand-ins
effect: A named low rank stands in for any card in a meld.
note: Canasta's twos. Simple, and it makes low ranks worth keeping.

name: Crazy Eights placement
effect: A card may only be placed adjacent to a card matching its suit or rank, and eights are wild and choose the suit.
note: Uno's rule as a placement restriction, which is a strong blind.

name: Draw until playable
effect: If nothing in the Entrance can be legally placed, draw until something can.
note: Mau Mau's rule, and the anti-softlock guarantee any restriction blind needs.

name: Chained penalties
effect: Certain ranks force the next placement to add extra cards, and the penalty chains if the next card is also one of them.
note: Switch's twos and fours. Escalating pressure that a player can pass along.

name: Sevens as foundations
effect: Sevens are the only cards placeable in an empty grid; everything else must build outward from them by rank in suit.
note: Fan Tan. A complete alternate placement ruleset in two sentences.

name: Trump suit
effect: One suit is named trump for the show; trump cards beat higher ranks of other suits in any comparison.
note: Whist's engine, and the cleanest way to make one suit matter for one night.

name: Trick taking
effect: The highest card of the leading suit in a line takes it - an alternate way to decide which card in a line scores.
note: Whist. A completely different reading of a five-card line.

name: The Booking
effect: Declare before the show exactly how many melds you will score; hit it exactly for a large bonus, miss it for nothing.
note: Oh Hell's bid, and the owner's own note that it belongs in this game. The alternative to bigger numbers.

name: Variable hand size
effect: Each show deals a different Entrance size, and the declaration scales with it.
note: Romanian Whist. Varies the whole texture of a show with one number.

name: Discard to bid
effect: Discard three cards to set your declaration - their suits determine the number you have committed to.
note: Ninety-Nine's elegant bid. The bid costs you the cards that made it.

name: Partner scoring
effect: Two-versus-two scoring, with special payouts for the pair.
note: Euchre and Spades. Only relevant if a co-op mode is ever built.

name: Auction for the trump
effect: Bid for the right to name the trump suit; the winner plays against everyone else.
note: Bridge's attacker-defender split, which suits an event more than a show.

name: Passing cards
effect: Pass cards from one grid's Entrance to another before placement begins.
note: Hearts' pass. A cross-grid verb available before any card is committed.

name: Negative melds
effect: A named suit scores zero, or negative, when it appears in a scored meld.
note: Hearts' queen of spades, and the owner's own note that this is a boss mechanic.

name: Pinochle melds
effect: Marriages of king and queen, the pinochle pairing, and sets of four - melds that care about specific cards, not shapes.
note: A different kind of meld: named cards rather than patterns.

name: Adjacency melds
effect: A marriage that requires the two cards to be exactly adjacent rather than merely in the same line.
note: Adjacency is a stronger constraint than line membership, and the grid makes it readable.

name: Priest and Clown marriage
effect: A themed adjacency meld between two specific classes.
note: Named melds give the class system something to aim at beyond counting.

name: Bid winner scores
effect: Only the declaring player may score melds; everyone else is defending.
note: Auction Pinochle. An asymmetric mode rather than a show rule.

name: Point cards
effect: Specific cards are worth specific points, and the bid is about capturing those.
note: Setback's structure. It makes individual cards matter more than shapes.

name: Cribbage counting
effect: Build a running total to thirty-one - ace one, faces ten, numbers face value - scoring for fifteens, pairs, and runs of three or more that need not be adjacent.
note: The full cribbage phase one, and the source of the rank-sum objectives.

name: Cribbage hand scoring
effect: Score the finished hand for fifteens, pairs, runs, four-card and five-card flushes, and a jack.
note: Phase two. The four-card flush is a meld the poker table has no equivalent of.

name: Climbing ranks
effect: Each card placed in a column must equal or exceed the rank of the one before it, with twos highest.
note: President's climb, and an excellent column restriction blind.

name: Matched multiples
effect: If the first placement of a refill is several cards of a rank, every later placement must match that count.
note: President's set-matching. Turns one choice into a constraint on the whole refill.

name: Saving low cards
effect: Holding pairs and triplets back to lead the next round is the real skill in climbing games.
note: A strategy note worth designing toward - the Entrance already permits it.

name: Scum tax
effect: The loser hands their two best cards to the winner before the next show.
note: President's scum rule. A brutal, memorable between-shows consequence.

name: Palace layout
effect: Three private cards, three face up and three face down, each set only playable once the previous is spent.
note: Palace. A three-tier reserve that suits the height coordinate exactly.

name: Twenty-one
effect: A line whose ranks total exactly twenty-one scores hugely; over twenty-one scores nothing.
note: Blackjack's bust rule as a line meld. Simple, tense and instantly understood.

name: Betting on the entrance
effect: Bet on the current Entrance against the next one, sight unseen.
note: Poker's real variety is information and betting, not melds - so import the betting.

name: Board game study
effect: The board-game channel survey that produced the entries below.
note: Reference.

name: Toll cells
effect: Certain cells must be paid for with a sacrificed card before they can be used.
note: Monopoly's properties. A blind that costs cards rather than points.

name: Tetromino melds
effect: Score for cards forming tetromino shapes, matched by suit or rank.
note: A shape meld that is neither row, column nor diagonal - the special bucket earns its keep.

name: Shape-request cells
effect: Some cells display a shape they want built on and around them, rotatable, and pay out when it is completed.
note: A cell objective the player can see and plan around, which is what a good blind does.

name: Pairs to thirteen
effect: Remove two adjacent cards whose ranks sum to thirteen, or which match.
note: Pyramid solitaire. A removal verb the one-way grid badly needs.

name: Entrance-matched removal
effect: Remove a placed card if it is one rank above or below a card in the Entrance.
note: Golf solitaire's rule, which makes the Entrance a tool rather than a queue.

name: Free cells
effect: Reserve cells outside the grid that hold one card each and can be reclaimed at any time.
note: FreeCell. The single most useful quality-of-life addition available.

name: Devil's Grip stacking
effect: Stacks build strictly by plus three in rank, and which row a card is in decides where its sequence starts.
note: An alternate stacking rule where position changes the arithmetic - unusually spatial.

name: Beehive swarm
effect: Four of a kind anywhere in a grid may be removed together for a bonus.
note: Beehive solitaire. A grid-wide set that ignores lines entirely.

name: Extreme rank values
effect: Ranks with bespoke point values - an ace worth one or eleven, a ten worth minus ten, a king worth ninety-nine.
note: The 31/99 family. Rank stops being a position and becomes a payout.

name: Loaned cards
effect: A temporary card that lasts a few shows and then leaves, or costs to keep.
note: Game of Life's loans. Rentals give the shop a cheap tier.

name: Sets of three
effect: Any three matching cards in a grid may be cashed for an escalating effect, such as a rank increase.
note: Risk's card sets. Escalation is what makes them worth saving for.

name: Sudoku bonus
effect: A grid whose ranks never repeat in any row or column scores an enormous bonus.
note: A whole-grid objective that fights every other incentive in the game, which is why it pays so much.

name: Minesweeper cells
effect: Grids are seeded with hidden bombs; cells show how many neighbours are mined, and placing on a bomb devalues the card.
note: Information as the counterplay. The best pure-hazard blind in the notes.

name: Hopping cards
effect: Cue to hop this card over an adjacent occupied cell into the empty one beyond.
note: Checkers. The frog card the draft names.

name: Decoder
effect: Sets a secret rank and suit; each placement reports whether it was wrong, right value in the wrong place, or exact.
note: Wordle in a grid. The first line to guess it correctly wins the bonus.

name: Three Ring Circus reference
effect: The board game whose cards care about their left and right neighbours and their types.
note: The nearest published relative of this game's adjacency scoring.

name: Neighbour typing
effect: Scores based on the types of the cards immediately left and right of it.
note: Three Ring Circus's core. The cheapest possible adjacency effect.

name: Ring class counts
effect: Several copies of one class or type in a single grid produce a special effect that scales with the count.
note: The autochess import, and the newest structural idea in the draft.

name: Effects read the board
effect: Rather than a separate class-bonus system, each effect checks the board itself and changes its own behaviour - the class synergy emerges from the cards.
note: The owner's own refinement, and the right one - no new system, and every card can carry its own scaling clause.

name: Adjacent-only entrance
effect: A boss Entrance that only permits placing a card next to a card already on the grid.
note: Poker Squares' own historical rule, weaponised. It makes the first placement enormously consequential.

name: Unique-line entrance
effect: A boss Entrance that requires every card to go in a column, or a row, no previously placed card has used.
note: The mirror restriction - it forces spread where the adjacent-only blind forces clumping.

name: Replay the show
effect: At show end, replay the whole round at speed as a highlight reel.
note: Cheap from the event log, and it turns a finished board into a story.

name: Cannon into cannon
effect: A card fired into a cell holding another cannon is fired again, chaining launches across grids until it lands somewhere empty.
note: The explicit ask. The chain is the fun, and cross-grid alignment is what makes it readable.

name: Piston
effect: Cue to push the entire row or column of cards one cell along, shunting whatever is at the end into the next grid.
note: Redstone-style pushing. The first effect that moves many cards with one verb.

name: Observer
effect: Fires whenever the card it faces changes - placed on, scored, moved or destroyed.
note: The trigger-on-neighbour-change primitive every chain machine needs.

name: Sticky piston
effect: Pushes a line of cards and pulls them back at the next refill.
note: Reversible movement, which makes a temporary formation possible.

name: The card flip
effect: Talent and art move to the top of the card and the pips to the bottom, so stacks build upward and scrolling rises with height.
note: Shipped as Phase 0. It puts the emphasis on the art and makes height read correctly.

name: Flipped score gutters
effect: Column and height scores flip with the card - columns read below the grid, heights above their own stacks.
note: Shipped. A height label sits above the stack it describes and rises as the stack grows.

name: Second pip row
effect: A second rank and suit beneath the art, with a second stamp slot for shoe or trouser equipment that never overlaps hat stamps.
note: Judged likely overkill in the same line - one item slot is enough, as Pokemon shows. Recorded, not adopted.

name: Lion
effect: Always counts as a king, whatever its printed rank.
note: A rank override with a face. Makes any card a face card for meld purposes.

name: Mirror Deck
effect: On entering the show, the deck doubles with temporary mirror copies of every card; a mirror placed next to its original destroys both.
note: A blind that doubles your resources and punishes you for using them carelessly. Excellent risk-reward shape.

name: Shy Clown
effect: May be returned to an empty Entrance slot, but only while the Entrance is attached to the grid it stands in.
note: The first card to make Entrance attachment mechanically visible, which is a genuinely new hook.

name: Show summary
effect: An end-of-show summary that records the best single play of the round.
note: Pairs with the replay. Naming your best play is what makes a run worth retelling.

name: Surrounding capture
effect: Cards fully surrounded by another suit or class are captured, Go-style.
note: A whole second way to interact with a placed board, and it needs no new coordinate.

name: Othello flipping
effect: Bracketing a line of cards between two of your own suit flips every card between them to that suit.
note: Reversi in a grid. The most dramatic single placement effect available.

name: Additional goals
effect: Every show carries an objective on top of the fame goal, and the number of objectives rises with difficulty alongside the score required.
note: The founding rule of the blinds category, stated by the owner.

name: Objective vocabulary
effect: The objective set - one empty tile, five pairs, a line summing between twenty and thirty, a matching rank in every grid, a row with no flush, one column ordered top to bottom, cards face down until placed.
note: The seven named objectives, each of which becomes its own blind row.

name: One effect per blind
effect: A blind chooses one effect; a boss blind gets one more. An effect may be a hazard rather than an objective.
note: The structural rule that keeps blinds composable instead of bespoke.

name: Candy-crush cells
effect: Some cells add to or subtract from the rank of whatever is placed on them.
note: The mancala cell, now with a blind to deploy it. The modifier is visible before you commit.

name: Suit-forcing cells
effect: Some cells demand a specific suit, or convert whatever is placed on them to that suit.
note: Two readings of the same cell - a restriction or a tool - and both are worth printing.

name: Auto-fill empty grids
effect: A grid you place nothing in this refill has a random card placed in it for you.
note: Punishes ignoring a grid, which is the dominant strategy without it.

name: Hidden opener
effect: The show begins with one face-down card already placed at random; it is only revealed when something is placed beside it.
note: Turns the empty grid into a question. Cheap, and it changes the first five placements.

name: Negative effects cost two
effect: A heavy negative such as losing a grid counts as two blind effects, and in exchange the remaining grids score double.
note: The weighting rule, and the owner's own alternative - losing score per cell used - is the more granular version.

name: Hazards must pay
effect: Every hazard must reward the player for playing into it rather than merely being a different level with no upside.
note: The design ruling every blind in the blinds file is written against.

name: Blinds per difficulty
effect: Difficulty adds one blind per three levels, so at difficulty four the third level of a set carries two.
note: The escalation formula, stated exactly.

name: Nuzlocke challenge
effect: A run-long challenge where every card added after the starting deck is locked in and can never be traded away.
note: Challenges sit above blinds - a blind is one level, a challenge is the whole run.

name: Named starting decks
effect: Specific decks the player chooses between at run start, restored as a first-class choice.
note: Restated in the newest lines, so it outranks the earlier ambivalence about deck unlocks.

name: Three node options
effect: Each step offers a talent pack, a trading hall or a special event.
note: Three is enough to choose between and few enough to read.

name: Vision to the nearest city
effect: The route is visible only as far as the closest city, so the player is never paralysed; effects extend the view.
note: The final word on fog of war, and it makes vision a purchasable advantage.

name: Balatro mod wikis
effect: The Balatro modding wiki and the Balatro wiki as sources for blind and joker design patterns.
note: Reference for the blinds category specifically - the newest draft names them for that reason.

name: Art-brief section breaks
effect: The rule lines separating the art brief's three parts - how the styles interact, why, and how to execute the fusion.
note: Document structure, kept so the brief stays readable as three sections rather than one wall.

name: Overhaul mandate
effect: The core-gameplay overhaul is done in its own worktree, with commits permitted there.
note: The working agreement for the whole stream.

name: The old system
effect: Five cards drawn into the Entrance dropped into six zones; the player built Klondike stacks and scoring ran at Submit over rows then columns.
note: SUPERSEDED in full. Recorded so the catalog can be audited against what actually changed.

name: The pivot
effect: A five-by-five grid replaces the zones; cards are placed by hand into empty cells; a filled row or column scores immediately; the five long diagonals count; every twenty-five to fifty cards of deck unlocks another grid; committing to a grid commits the whole Entrance to it.
note: The overhaul in one paragraph. Shipped.

name: Two view modes
effect: Each grid gets its own panel; the player switches between a zoomed-out view of every grid and a focused view of one. The Entrance follows the focused grid until placement commits it.
note: Phase 6 work, not yet built. The geometry it pans over is now stable.

name: Wide picture
effect: The scene must be wide enough for three grids, centred, so the picture on the wall is very wide and the camera sees only part of it.
note: Shipped in the wall's picture sizing.

name: Panning between grids
effect: Left and right buttons, swipes or shoulder buttons pan between grids, always snapping a grid to centre with none cut off; the all-grids view hides the wall and its frame, and the wall's saved pan is treated as a camera position in real space.
note: Phase 6. The saved pan is what makes the picture wall and the board agree.

name: End without scoring
effect: Submit becomes End - it fires its hooks and finishes the show without a scoring round, and may be pressed with the board unfinished. Cards bow or jump on the way out.
note: Shipped, minus the bow animation, which is still a todo.

name: Placement is one-way
effect: Once placed, a card cannot be moved or stacked on by default; both are reserved for effects.
note: Shipped. Every movement card in this file is an exception the player buys.

name: Rows align across grids
effect: Row one of every grid sits at the same y across the whole screen, which is what lets an effect say move five cells left and land in the same cell of the grid to the left.
note: Shipped, with a setting to keep grids aligned when one grows taller than another.

name: The four-coordinate
effect: A board position is grid, x, y and height.
note: Shipped as BoardCoord. Comparison is by equals, never by the identity operator.

name: Total in the HUD
effect: The running total stays in the HUD as the grid labels update, so the player never has to add up.
note: Shipped.

name: Compaction
effect: Removing a card from a stack drops everything above it down one.
note: Shipped. Dropping down never retriggers scoring.

name: Rescoring on rebuild
effect: Removing a card from a completed line and replacing it fires the scoring event again.
note: Shipped. It is why rescoring effects have to be costed carefully.

name: The test mandate
effect: Build one grid a card at a time up to a full fifteen-high stack in all twenty-five cells, detect every line of five, in many orders, with random moves, removals and fuzz.
note: Shipped as the grid test suites. Stacking rules are ignored in these tests on purpose.

name: Misalignment setting
effect: A setting that makes every grid expand its rows when one grid grows taller.
note: Shipped, defaulting off, with a test proving the same board scores identically either way.

name: Standard test deck
effect: A plain fifty-two card deck exists for testing the new setup.
note: Shipped.

name: Recycle everything
effect: The overhaul updates state and rules cards rather than deleting systems, because few effects were hardcoded to the tableau and the old design survives as stacking on top of the grid.
note: Vindicated - the class survived the pivot intact.

name: Scoring after every move
effect: Scoring runs after every card move, driven by a rule card that checks for a new completed line containing the moved card's position.
note: Shipped as SkillLineDetector.

name: Drop-down removed
effect: No drop-down logic, whether by zone or by the Next button.
note: Shipped - removed.

name: New state arrays
effect: State gains the arrays it needs to track grids of cells of cards, and the score trackers to match.
note: Shipped as GridData plus the coordinate-keyed score buckets.

name: No Next button
effect: The Next button goes with the drop-down.
note: Shipped.

name: Entrance follows then sticks
effect: Entrance cards follow the focused grid until a card is placed, then stay attached to that grid.
note: Shipped in the data; the follow animation is Phase 6.

name: Grid allotment card
effect: A rule card that counts the deck at game start and adds one grid-creation card per twenty-five cards.
note: Shipped as SkillGridAllotment.

name: Grid creation card
effect: When active it creates the twenty-five cell cards it owns; when inactive it removes them and discards their contents, following the zone-creation card's logic.
note: Shipped as SkillGridCreator.

name: Random entrance refill
effect: Five Entrance cards as before, but a refill fills slots in random order rather than left to right, so the first slot is not always first.
note: Shipped. The first Entrance card still aligns with the first column.

name: Line detector card
effect: A rule card that detects a new line of five anywhere across the grids and scores it.
note: Shipped as SkillLineDetector.

name: Art frame reuse
effect: New rule cards use unused frames from the existing art sheets; cards that no longer work are archived rather than deleted.
note: Shipped, and the archive is what the catalog's superseded rows are for.

name: Iterator across grids
effect: The iterator walks Entrance cards left to right, then each grid in turn - leftmost first, left slot of the top row, down the rows - then the discard and the rule deck.
note: Shipped, with the order pinned by tests.

name: Retire stale rule cards
effect: Rule cards that no longer apply are removed from the deck.
note: Shipped. The zone-only cards remain in a ratcheted test list rather than in the deck.

name: Ask what was missed
effect: The design must say plainly what high-level changes the braindump did not mention.
note: The instruction that produced the gap protocol.

name: The documentation mandate
effect: Alternate updated versions of every design document and CSV, the draft re-read and appended, a new accepted-ideas CSV mined from the design docs, the catalog's seen column reset, and no other doc left describing the old design.
note: This file, the blinds file, the accepted-ideas file and the catalog rewrite are the deliverable.

name: Sandwich
effect: When this card scores, gain a point for every card between it and the nearest same-suit card further down its stack.
note: Renamed Sliced Bread in the draft. Height is what makes it visible.

name: Selection Sort
effect: Moves up one place in its stack whenever the card above it has a lower rank.
note: A stack that sorts itself over several refills. Deeply satisfying to watch.

name: More Poker
effect: Poker hands score double.
note: The plainest amplifier in the game, and the one every costing model should be calibrated against.

name: Spaceship
effect: May be placed in the void - outside any grid, where it still counts for cross-grid lines.
note: The void is now a real place: the gap between grids. This card lives in it.

name: Self-Placing Card
effect: While in the deck, if a legal empty cell ever exists, this card moves itself there.
note: A card that plays itself, which is unsettling in exactly the right way.

name: Recycler
effect: On score, put two random cards from the discard back into the deck; Exhaust cards do not return.
note: Anti-thinning, which is a real cost in an economy that pays in cards.

name: Egg
effect: When this card scores, it becomes a completely different random card of higher rank.
note: A card that is worth more after you use it, which nothing else does.

name: Champion
effect: Cards of the same rank directly above or below this card in its stack are discarded.
note: Anti-pair, which fights the pair objectives directly. Good tension.

name: All In
effect: On the next score, double the total - and double the fame the next show demands.
note: Borrowing against the future, which is the Hype wager as a card.

name: Deja Vu
effect: Remembers the cell it was placed in; the next time that cell is empty, it returns there from anywhere.
note: A card with a home. The grid gives it a coordinate to remember at last.

name: Rabbit
effect: If this card is grabbed, it bolts to the furthest orthogonal cell instead.
note: Comic, and a genuine obstacle - you have to plan around a card that will not be caught.

name: Robber
effect: Between refills, robbers steal the highest-value card from the board.
note: A recurring theft the player can bait with a decoy, which is the counterplay.

name: Trap
effect: Creates an extra empty cell; the next card placed there goes underneath this card instead, and the extra cell disappears.
note: Insertion beneath, which the upward stack makes strange and useful.

name: Goalpost
effect: Enhances a random viable meld type, chosen fresh each show.
note: The trending-meld idea as a card rather than a rule.

name: Distancing
effect: Hovers at the top of its stack without blocking the card beneath it, and cannot be clicked.
note: The Ghost Light stamp's ancestor, and it may count as its own row.

name: Pot of Greed
effect: When this card is alone in its grid's row, discard it and draw two.
note: Conditional on isolation, which the empty-tile objective loves and everything else hates.

name: Rewrite
effect: Remembers the cards beneath it when placed; at show end it replaces that many cards below it with fresh draws.
note: A delayed board rewrite. Expensive to reason about, which is why it is Epic.

name: Paintbrush
effect: Cards this one is placed on take its suit.
note: The Clown class's suit fixer, applied downward through a stack.

name: The One Ring
effect: You always know exactly where this card is; destroy it permanently and win the show outright.
note: An alternate win condition that the destruction family has to work for.

name: Lightning
effect: Lightning strikes the highest-value card on the board, shocking it and everything adjacent.
note: Punishes concentrating value in one cell, which is otherwise always correct.

name: No Part of Any Hand
effect: If this card is in no scoring hand at all, it pays a large flat bonus.
note: The anti-meld card, and the empty-chair objective's best friend.

name: Parasite
effect: Attaches to the next card placed on top of it; at show end it replaces its host entirely.
