note: A card scoring for standing adjacent to something that could destroy it.

name: Whiteface and Auguste
effect: The elegant whiteface commands and the auguste bungles; by legend, Tom Belling created the auguste by accident.
note: The two-clown hierarchy that the paired clown card is built on.

name: The Entree
effect: Structured clown scenes built to a payoff gag - clown combos are scripted sequences rather than single triggers.
note: Ordered quests, in the Clown class's own vocabulary.

name: Grock reference
effect: The Swiss king of clowns, whose musical virtuosity was perpetually defeated by furniture.
note: Provenance for the Grock card.

name: Charlie Rivel
effect: Akrobat schoen - the chair, the guitar and the wail.
note: A clown card and its audio cue in one reference.

name: Slava's Snowshow
effect: The blizzard finale that buries the audience in snow and joy.
note: The best possible model for an end-of-show celebration.

name: Weary Willie cross-reference
effect: The Depression hobo who never smiled is specced in the recommendations.
note: A pointer row.

name: Sacred Clowns
effect: Heyoka and Pueblo koshare - contrary ritual clowns who do everything backwards, sacred rather than comic.
note: Recorded with its caveat: this is ceremony, not a gag to lift.

name: Kyogen
effect: Comic interludes between solemn Noh plays.
note: A small comic bonus round between shows, which paces a long tour.

name: Pierrot
effect: The whitefaced moon-mad lover of French pantomime.
note: A card that buffs at night, on the alternate night-show rule.

name: Pagliacci
effect: The clown who must perform while his heart breaks.
note: A card that scores more the worse the show is going.

name: Guignol
effect: France's Punch, whose satire was sharp enough that police monitored the scripts.
note: A censored level where certain card text is redacted until played.

name: Rodeo clown cross-reference
effect: The protector clown is catalogued under the Americas and cross-referenced here.
note: A pointer row.

name: Isaac Fawkes
effect: The 1720s fairground conjurer who died rich on the egg bag and the blooming apple tree.
note: A card that produces cards indefinitely and made its owner wealthy - the economy engine with a face.

name: Matthew Buchinger
effect: Born without hands or legs; a virtuoso magician, marksman and micrographic calligrapher who hid psalms inside the curls of his own portrait.
note: A card with a secret written into its art, discoverable only by looking closely.

name: Robert-Houdin
effect: The watchmaker who invented modern magic - evening dress instead of robes, mechanical marvels, and the whole grammar of the stage.
note: The Magician leader, and the clockwork theme's origin.

name: Magic as Statecraft
effect: Robert-Houdin was sent to Algeria in 1856 to out-miracle the marabouts.
note: An event where your show is used politically, and you choose whether to play along.

name: The Great Wizard of the North
effect: John Henry Anderson, a pioneer of publicity, ruined three times by theatre fires and rebuilding each time.
note: A card that returns stronger after each run it loses.

name: Egyptian Hall
effect: Maskelyne and Cooke's England's Home of Mystery, which ran for three decades and exposed fake spiritualists as part of the act.
note: A permanent venue node that also disables deception cards.

name: All Done By Kindness
effect: David Devant, the gentlest master, and his motto.
note: The flavour text for a card that only ever buffs.

name: Adelaide Herrmann
effect: The great Herrmann died mid-tour and Adelaide took over the show, performing for decades after.
note: A leader who inherits - when your leader is lost, this one takes the run over.

name: The Royal Succession
effect: Kellar publicly passed his mantle to Thurston on stage - America's magic royal succession.
note: A meta-progression where a retired card names its heir.

name: Soo versus Foo
effect: The American imitator against the Chinese original, a rivalry of billing, imitation and challenge.
note: The Rival Show blind, with the uncomfortable history intact.

name: Harry Blackstone Sr
effect: The vanishing birdcage and the floating lightbulb - and the night he calmly evacuated a burning theatre by pretending it was part of the act.
note: A card that turns a disaster into a performance and scores for it.

name: Cardini
effect: Endless fans of cards materialising at the fingertips of a bemused, tipsy gentleman.
note: A card that produces another card every refill and appears surprised each time.

name: The Ambitious Card
effect: Dai Vernon fooled Houdini seven times in 1922 with a card that keeps returning to the top of the deck.
note: The deck-position family's signature card, and the best story in card magic.

name: The Bamberg Dynasty
effect: Six unbroken generations of magicians, from the seventeenth century to the twentieth.
note: A dynasty save file - a lineage that persists across runs.

name: The Zancigs
effect: Two Minds with but a Single Thought - a husband-and-wife second-sight code act.
note: Two cards in different grids that share information and score together.

name: Arthur Lloyd
effect: The Human Card Index, who could produce any requested card or document from his forty pockets.
note: The perfect tutor, already drafted from the game notes and confirmed here.

name: P T Selbit
effect: Invented sawing a woman in half in 1921, and walking through a wall.
note: Provenance for two cards the draft already names.

name: Richiardi Jr
effect: The sawing played as grand guignol - visible gore, stunned silence, then the reveal.
note: A town that rewards showmanship at its most extreme, and punishes restraint.

name: Channing Pollock
effect: The elegant dove worker who made bird production high art.
note: A card that produces an Animal token each time it scores.

name: The Wonder Era
effect: Doug Henning's 1970s revival, which framed magic as wonder and joy rather than as a challenge.
note: A meta-set name, and a tonal alternative to the deception cards.

name: Vanishing the Statue
effect: Copperfield vanished the Statue of Liberty in 1983 - the largest illusion ever staged.
note: Remove an entire grid from view for one refill, and bring it back untouched.

name: Penn and Teller principle
effect: Explaining the trick and still fooling you - the cups and balls performed with clear cups.
note: A design principle: full information can be more astonishing than concealment. It argues for showing the rules.

name: Ricky Jay
effect: Card-throwing lethality, fifty-two assistants, and the scholarship of forgotten performers.
note: A card thrown as a weapon along a row, which is the knife suit with a deck instead.

name: The Exposure Taboo
effect: Magic's governing secrecy norm - exposure gets you expelled.
note: A rule card that penalises revealing hidden cards, which gives the info family a real cost.

name: The Fox Sisters
effect: Spiritualism was born in 1848 from two girls cracking their toe joints, and Margaret confessed forty years later.
note: A card whose enormous effect is revealed as a trick, and stops working once exposed.

name: The Spirit Cabinet
effect: The Davenport brothers, tied inside a cabinet while instruments played by spirits - and Maskelyne exposed it.
note: A card that works only while it is covered and bound.

name: Spirit Photography
effect: Mumler's double-exposure ghosts, and cheesecloth ectoplasm - a card that shows a faint copy of a card removed from play.
note: Fakery that produces something genuinely useful, which is the Gaff family's best form.

name: The Ouija Board
effect: The parlour talking board, patented in 1891, which became an industry.
note: A consumable that answers one question about the deck, ambiguously.

name: Houdini versus Margery
effect: The Scientific American prize committee, the Boston medium, and magic's most famous investigation.
note: A deduction event with a prize for exposing the fake.

name: Midnight Spook Shows
effect: Travelling theatre ghost-blackout shows, before horror films took the audience.
note: The Ghost Show secret, sourced.

name: X-Ray Eyes
effect: Kuda Bux, the fire-walker whose blindfold act was billed as X-ray vision - this card sees the board while it is itself covered.
note: Another anti-spotlight card, and information as the reward for being buried.

name: Clever Hans
effect: The counting horse who was actually reading his questioner's body language, and gave his name to an experimental effect.
note: A card that answers correctly only while a specific other card is adjacent.

name: The Learned Pig
effect: Eighteenth and nineteenth century sensations - pigs that spelled, read minds and told the time.
note: An Animal card that performs an information effect, which no other Animal card does.

name: The Turk
effect: Von Kempelen's chess automaton, which beat Napoleon and Franklin with a hidden operator inside.
note: A card whose effect is actually performed by the card hidden beneath it.

name: The Digesting Duck
effect: Vaucanson's mechanical duck that ate and digested - except the digestion was pre-loaded.
note: A consumption card that does not really consume, and returns what it took.

name: Karakuri cross-reference
effect: The Edo automata are catalogued under Japan.
note: A pointer row.

name: Phantasmagoria
effect: Magic-lantern ghosts projected on smoke in a Capuchin crypt in 1790s Paris - projection as terror.
note: The oldest ancestor of the effect-art pop-up.

name: Pepper's Ghost
effect: The 1862 angled-glass reflection illusion, still how holograms of dead musicians work.
note: A ghost-card visual that is a reflection rather than a sprite.

name: Pre-Cinema Spectacle
effect: Magic lanterns, panoramas, cycloramas and the Eidophusikon - immersive picture-spectacles before film.
note: The picture wall's ancestors, and a reason it is the right metaphor.

name: The Raree Box
effect: Itinerant viewing-boxes offering a private glimpse for a coin.
note: A consumable that reveals one thing to you alone.

name: Waxworks
effect: Madame Tussaud's death-mask realism as touring spectacle, and the Chamber of Horrors.
note: The Wax type, sourced - it melts near Flames because wax does.

name: Zoltar
effect: Coin-op prophecy cabinets of the penny arcade.
note: A machine that sells you one prediction per show.

name: Flea circus cross-reference
effect: Real harnessed fleas pulling chariots, already specced in the recommendations.
note: A pointer row.

name: Mamluk Cards
effect: Cups, swords, coins and polo-sticks crossed from Egypt into Europe's suits.
note: The historical origin of suits, and a visual set for an alternate deck.

name: The French Suit Revolution
effect: Flat two-colour suits made cards cheap to print, and the pack was democratised.
note: Production cost as a design force - the reason four suits won.

name: Named Court Cards
effect: French tradition names every face - the King of Spades is David, of Hearts Charlemagne.
note: Face cards with individual identities, which the Joey and Ringmistress ideas reach for.

name: The Ace of Spades
effect: English decks paid duty through an ornate official ace, and forging it was a hanging offence.
note: A stamp that proves a card is legitimate, and a Forged Ace that pretends.

name: The Joker
effect: Born as Euchre's Best Bower, the deck's newest card, later adopted by magicians and printers as a signature.
note: The wild rank, with its actual history rather than its assumed one.

name: Trionfi
effect: Tarot trumps were a game for three hundred years before an invented Egyptian mythology turned them into fortune-telling.
note: The Major Arcana consumables, with the honest history attached.

name: Card game cross-references
effect: Hanafuda, karuta and ganjifa are catalogued under Japan and India.
note: A pointer row.

name: The Holdout
effect: The Kepplinger sleeve machine - a mechanical arm delivering palmed cards on cue.
note: A card held outside the deck and produced exactly when wanted.

name: The Cooler
effect: A pre-stacked deck swapped into play.
note: Replace your remaining deck with a known order, once per run.

name: Marked
effect: Marked cards, shiners, second and bottom dealing - the card sharp's quiet arts.
note: You always know where this card is in the deck.

name: Erdnase cross-reference
effect: The unknown author of the card-handling bible is specced in the recommendations.
note: A pointer row.

name: Bucking the Tiger
effect: Faro, the Old West's dominant game, so widely rigged that honest faro was the exception.
note: The Faro Bank blind, sourced.

name: Three-Card Monte
effect: The eternal street hustle, in which the mark never wins.
note: Already specced as the Pie Car's game. The honest version is that you cannot win it.

name: George Devol
effect: The Mississippi riverboat sharp of Forty Years a Gambler, who head-butted opponents like a battering ram.
note: A Gambler leader whose signature is that losses cost less.

name: Dead Man's Hand
effect: Aces and eights, held by Wild Bill Hickok when he was shot in Deadwood in 1876.
note: A secret meld that pays enormously and destroys the card that completed it.

name: Poker Alice
effect: The frontier's famous female dealers - Poker Alice and Madame Moustache.
note: A Gambler leader for a gambling-focused deck.

name: Canfield's House Game
effect: Richard Canfield sold the deck for fifty dollars and paid five per card placed - the house always won.
note: A shop where you buy your own deck back a card at a time. Brutal, historical and legible.

name: Klondike
effect: The most famous solitaire, named for the gold fields.
note: A gold-rush biome name with a solitaire attached.

name: Napoleon's Patience
effect: Legend has the exiled emperor playing patience on Saint Helena, and several patiences bear his name.
note: A named deck, and a story about playing alone.

name: Escape Map Decks
effect: The US Playing Card Company hid escape maps inside cards sent to prisoner-of-war camps in the Second World War.
note: A card that reveals a hidden route on the map when peeled apart, once.

name: Cardistry
effect: Card flourishing as pure visual art.
note: The shuffle and draw animations, elevated into their own reward.

name: The Mitt Camp
effect: Palmistry, tasseography and phrenology - the midway's pseudo-sciences.
note: Fortune Teller class flavour, with the honest note that none of it worked.

name: The Brass Ring
effect: Carousel riders grabbed at a brass ring for a free ride, an idea born from cavalry lance training.
note: Reach out from a moving card to claim a bonus - the origin of grabbing the brass ring.

name: The Midway
effect: Both the Ferris wheel and the word midway come from the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition.
note: The shop row's proper name.

name: Ice Slides
effect: Catherine the Great's ice mountains became the scenic railway and then the roller coaster.
note: A biome name with a lineage.

name: The Ghost Train
effect: The tunnel-of-fright fairground staple - a blind node whose effect is not revealed until you are inside.
note: A blind you accept without seeing, for a larger reward.

name: Hall of Mirrors
effect: Distortion as delight - the boss show duplicates every effect into the mirrored grid.
note: Already written into the blinds file; this is its source.

name: The Arcade
effect: Penny arcades and mutoscopes - coin-operated amusement rows.
note: A node of minigames that reuse the solitaire engine.

name: The Lecture
effect: Barnum-style storefront dime museums, with lecturers narrating the oddities.
note: An event that explains one hidden rule permanently.

name: Exposition City
effect: The mega-expositions every showman orbited, from the Crystal Palace onward.
note: Already written into the blinds file; this is its source.

name: The Unicorn
effect: Pre-zoo travelling menageries, including a one-horned rhinoceros billed as a unicorn.
note: An Animal card billed as something it is not, and worth more for the billing.

name: Resort Towns
effect: Blackpool, the piers and Tivoli - Europe's permanent pleasure grounds.
note: Nodes with lower goals and better shops, for a run that needs a breather.

name: The Kickline
effect: The Moulin Rouge cancan - the kickline as scandal and spectacle.
note: A full row of Dancer cards scoring in unison.

name: Wintergarten
effect: The Berlin variety palace where the Skladanowsky brothers premiered projected cinema in 1895.
note: The node where a new technology arrives and changes the rules.

name: The Rat Sheet
effect: Circuses printed attack-posters slandering rival shows ahead of them.
note: A consumable that weakens the next Rival Show.

name: Day and Date
effect: Two rival circuses booking the same town on the same day - billing war at its hottest.
note: Already written into the blinds file; this is its source.

name: The Patch
effect: The show's legal adjuster, smoothing and bribing local officials.
note: A consumable that cancels one blind before it applies.

name: The 24-Hour Man
effect: The advance agent marking tomorrow's route on poles and fences.
note: Reveals the next node's blind a show early.

name: At Liberty
effect: The trade-paper ad meaning a performer is unemployed and hireable.
note: A pool of cards other runs discarded, available cheap.

name: The Cookhouse Flag
effect: When the flag flew, the lot ate - the day's heartbeat.
note: A mid-show pause that restores a resource.

name: Working Slang
effect: Cherry pie, cutting up jackpots, First of May, kinker, towner, gilly and jump - the trade's own vocabulary.
note: A whole naming layer that costs nothing and reads as authentic because it is.

name: The Candy Butcher
effect: Aisle vendors, and lemonade sold as juice.
note: Concessions-class naming.

name: The Disaster March
effect: Stars and Stripes Forever was played only to signal catastrophe and start the evacuation.
note: An audio cue the player learns to dread, which is the most efficient tension in the file.

name: Entrance of the Gladiators
effect: The circus tune, originally a serious military march by Fucik in 1897.
note: The theme, and the fact that it was not written as a joke.

name: Screamer Marches
effect: The breakneck circus-band genre, of which Barnum and Bailey's Favorite is the type specimen.
note: The tempo reference for the scoring animation.

name: The Band Organ
effect: Steam-whistle music heard miles ahead, and punched-book fairground organs.
note: The map's audio identity, and the Calliope card's instrument.

name: Showmen's Rest
effect: The Woodlawn cemetery plot where the dead of the 1918 Hagenbeck-Wallace train wreck lie, ringed by elephant statues.
note: The Dead List's real-world counterpart, and a secret worth finding once.

name: Deus ex Machina
effect: The Greek crane lowering a god to untangle the plot, criticised as a cheat for two and a half thousand years.
note: A card that resolves an unwinnable board, and is openly a cheat.

name: The Greek Chorus
effect: The ensemble that watches, comments and warns - inside the story and outside it.
note: A card that scores for what other cards do without ever acting itself.

name: Thalia and Melpomene
effect: The comedy and tragedy masks, worn as one symbol.
note: A card with two effects, one for a winning board and one for a losing one.

name: The City Dionysia
effect: Athens' playwright competition, where drama was a judged contest with civic prizes.
note: A judged event where several objectives are ranked rather than passed or failed.

name: The Claque
effect: Professional paid applauders, institutionalised by the Paris opera, where chefs de claque sold applause by the row.
note: Already written into the blinds file; this is its source.

name: The Loggione
effect: La Scala's merciless connoisseur gallery, which has booed the world's greatest singers.
note: Already written into the blinds file; this is its source.

name: The Prima Donna
effect: The diva whose demands reorganise the whole company - the strongest card scores double and every other card scores less.
note: A card that is worth building around and painful to build around.

name: The Scottish Play
effect: Saying Macbeth inside a theatre invites the curse, and the cleansing ritual is to spin three times and swear.
note: A superstition rule card with a literal undo ritual attached.

name: The Whistling Ban
effect: Stage rigging was run by ex-sailors on whistle codes, so a stray whistle could drop a sandbag.
note: A rule where a specific action has a rare catastrophic consequence, for real historical reasons.

name: Break a Leg
effect: The theatre's inverted luck-language - wishing good is bad, so wish bad.
note: The vocabulary for a card that pays out on failure.

name: The Encore Exit
effect: Leave the stage, be called back, return bigger - voluntarily discard this card to have it return next refill at double value.
note: The encore as a mechanic rather than as a chance.

name: The Standing Ovation
effect: The full house on its feet - the show's highest verdict.
note: The perfect-show reward's name.

name: He's Behind You
effect: British panto's sacred contract - the crowd screams warnings the performer pretends not to hear.
note: A card that is warned about an incoming hazard and may choose to ignore it.

name: Melodrama
effect: Mustache-twirling villains, sawmills and train tracks - morality as spectacle, with the audience booing on cue.
note: A level with an explicit villain card the player must beat rather than outscore.

name: The Pledge the Turn the Prestige
effect: The three-act grammar of a trick - show the ordinary thing, make it extraordinary, bring it back.
note: A three-stage scoring effect, which is the ordered-quest shape with a name everyone knows.

name: Kayfabe
effect: The never-broken pretence that the show is real, protected for a century like a trade secret, and carnival cant by origin.
note: A rule card under which every Gaff and fake counts as genuine.

name: Faces and Heels
effect: Heroes and villains as assigned, swappable roles - the crowd needs both.
note: An alignment axis orthogonal to class, and cheap to add.

name: Heat
effect: Crowd hatred that sells tickets, and cheap heat earned by insulting the local team.
note: A second currency earned by being disliked, which nothing else in the game produces.

name: The Heel Turn
effect: The beloved hero's betrayal - the loudest story wrestling tells.
note: A card that flips alignment mid-run and rewrites its own effect.

name: The Cheap Pop
effect: It is great to be here in your town - instant applause, every night, in every city.
note: A small guaranteed bonus that works once per node and never gets old.

name: The Belt
effect: The championship as physical lineage - held, defended and taken.
note: Exactly one exists per run, and it moves to whoever beats its holder.

name: The Jobber
effect: The designated losers - the Washington Generals lost over thirteen thousand games to the Globetrotters.
note: A card whose job is to lose, and which pays the card that beats it.

name: The Montreal Screwjob
effect: The scripted world broke live on air when the promoter really double-crossed the champion.
note: An event where the game's own rules betray you once, deliberately.

name: The Blind Spot
effect: The folding chair behind the referee's back - cheating as choreography.
note: A card that may break one rule while a specific other card is not looking.

name: The Manager
effect: The talker who carries the silent monster's story - this card cues the card beside it.
note: Delegated activation, which the charge system already supports.

name: Mascara contra Mascara
effect: Mask against mask - the loser is unmasked forever, and El Santo was buried in his.
note: A duel with a permanent stake, which is the highest one the game can offer.

name: Tecnicos and Rudos
effect: Lucha's alignment pair - clean technique against glorious cheating.
note: The alignment axis's better-sounding names.

name: The Streak
effect: A win streak so mythic that its ending was the story of the decade.
note: A run-long counter whose value is entirely in not breaking it.

name: To Be the Man
effect: The title chase as philosophy - to be the man, you have to beat the man.
note: The belt-challenge objective's name.

name: The Crowd Surf
effect: Trust the crowd or eat the floor - pass a card across the tops of several stacks.
note: Traversal along the top of a board rather than through it.

name: Brown M and Ms
effect: Van Halen's rider clause existed to test whether venues had actually read the safety requirements.
note: A card that detects whether a blind was read - and warns you if it was not.

name: The Soundcheck
effect: The invisible crew and the empty-hall rehearsal before doors.
note: A preview turn where placements can be tried and taken back.

name: Encore cross-reference
effect: The encore ritual is catalogued under theatre.
note: A pointer row.

name: Lighters Up
effect: The audience becomes the light show during the slow song.
note: A crowd visual that responds to the board rather than to the score.

name: Woodstock
effect: The fences fell, half a million came, nobody paid, and it became the legend of the century.
note: An event that costs you every token and pays you fame instead.

name: Fyre Festival
effect: The luxury festival that did not exist - influencer hype, relief tents and the sad cheese sandwich.
note: The Scam Booking blind, sourced.

name: The Skip
effect: Milli Vanilli's lip-sync scandal, and the Grammy revoked after the tape skipped.
note: An event where a card is exposed as a copy and removed.

name: Eurovision
effect: Bloc voting, douze points, and national camp as song-contest diplomacy.
note: The international node, judged by several towns at once.

name: The Pitch Ballot
effect: Licensed buskers ballot for timeslots at Covent Garden's best pitches.
note: An event where you draw for position rather than for cards.

name: The Hat
effect: If you liked the show - the ask is a craft of its own.
note: Converting combo into tips at the end of a show, by asking well.

name: Ball Culture
effect: Competitive walking in judged categories, with houses as chosen families.
note: A node judged by category rather than by score, and a class structure with real warmth.

name: Reading
effect: The stylized roast - reading is the real art form.
note: The duel system's ballroom skin.

name: The Pose
effect: Voguing - battle dance built from magazine poses, frozen glamour as combat.
note: Hold a formation for a refill to score it again.

name: Lip Sync for Your Life
effect: The bottom two duel, the winner stays, the loser sashays away.
note: An elimination duel between two of your own cards.

name: The Cypher
effect: Breaking crew battles in the circle, from the Bronx to the 2024 Olympics.
note: The duel system's hip-hop skin, and its only competitive-sport form.

name: The Cutting Contest
effect: Tap dancers trading escalating breaks - the Nicholas Brothers ended arguments by being better.
note: The duel system's tap skin, and the escalation model for all of them.

name: Butoh
effect: The post-war dance of darkness - white-painted, glacially slow, transformative.
note: A card that changes by one small degree every refill and is unrecognisable by the end.

name: Jugalbandi
effect: The virtuoso duet-duel - dancer answers drummer, call and response, neither yielding.
note: The duel system's Indian skin, and the one that ends in harmony rather than a winner.

name: Marcel Marceau
effect: Bip, the world's mime - and before that a Resistance member who used mime to keep hidden children silent as he led them to safety.
note: A card that escorts other cards safely past a hazard. One of the five stories worth full flavour text.

name: The Invisible Wall
effect: The mime's constructed nothing - block one column against every effect, including your own.
note: A wall made of an agreement, which is the most theatrical protection in the file.

name: Edgar Bergen
effect: A ventriloquist who became the number one act on radio - a skill rendered pointless by the medium, and a star anyway.
note: A card whose stated advantage does not apply and which scores regardless.

name: The Throw
effect: Making the voice live somewhere else - cue a card's effect to resolve at a different cell.
note: Relocating an effect without relocating its card.

name: The Nantes Giants
effect: Building-sized marionettes walked through cities by teams of Lilliputians on ropes.
note: A card so large it occupies several cells and is moved by the cards around it.

name: War Horse
effect: Puppets so alive the audience grieves for plywood and cane.
note: The belief threshold - the animation target for making a card feel like a performer.

name: Bread and Puppet
effect: Political parade puppetry that hands out free bread - art is cheap and everyone should have it.
note: An event that gives cards away for nothing and asks nothing back.

name: The Statue
effect: The street performer who scores by not moving - this card gains points for every refill it is untouched.
note: The counterweight to a board that rewards constant action.

name: The One-Man Band
effect: Cymbals between the knees and a harmonica in the rack - everything at once, none of it well.
note: A card that fires several effects, each at reduced strength.

name: Keaton's Falling Wall
effect: A two-ton facade falls on him and he survives through one open window, on a set measured to inches.
note: A hazard that destroys everything except one cell, which is shown in advance.

name: The Clock Hang
effect: Harold Lloyd dangling from a clock face above the street - the defining image of silent comedy.
note: A card placed half off the edge of a grid, scoring in both the grid and the gap.

name: The Seven Little Fortunes
effect: The brutal Peking Opera academy that forged Jackie Chan, Sammo Hung and Yuen Biao.
note: The Academy meta-structure - cards trained rather than bought, at a cost.

name: The Stunt Double
effect: Yakima Canutt invented modern stunt craft, including the Ben-Hur chariot race, so that stars could survive their own films.
note: A card that takes a destructive effect in another card's place.

name: The Demolition Show
effect: Monster trucks and demolition derby - destruction as the whole show.
note: A show scored entirely on cards destroyed rather than on lines completed.

name: Aquamusicals
effect: Sonja Henie's ice shows and Esther Williams' aquamusicals rebuilt skating and swimming as spectacle industries.
note: Precedent for a whole alternate board surface - ice or water - with its own physics.

name: Guy Laliberte
effect: A fire-breathing stilt-walker busking in Quebec who built the world's biggest circus and then bought a seat on a rocket.
note: The busker-to-space progression arc, as a leader whose scaling never stops.

name: Nouveau Cirque
effect: Circus stripped of glitter and animals - chainsaws, narrative and rock music.
note: A deck with no Animal cards and a much harder edge.

name: David Blaine
effect: Buried alive, frozen in ice, forty-four days fasting in a box over the Thames - the hunger artist with a live feed.
note: An endurance card that scores for refills survived doing nothing.

name: The System
effect: Derren Brown's guaranteed tipster, revealed as survivorship bias - he filmed every branch and showed you only the winning one.
note: A card that appears infallible because you never see its failures.

name: The Million Dollar Challenge
effect: James Randi's standing prize for provable paranormal ability, never claimed.
note: A run-long objective nobody has completed, kept as a genuine open bounty.

name: Controlled Props
effect: Carson, an ex-magician briefed by Randi, supplied his own props and the spoon-bending did not happen.
note: A card that neutralises a deception card by insisting on its own conditions.

name: Shin Lim
effect: Close-up card magic - just cards - winning the biggest talent show on television.
note: A card with no props, no class synergies and an enormous ceiling.

name: The Golden Buzzer
effect: One judge's press sends an act straight through, with confetti falling.
note: Skip a node and take its reward.

name: The Gong Show
effect: Gonged mid-act - failure as the entertainment.
note: The Gong blind, sourced.

name: The Masked Singer
effect: Celebrities perform masked, and the weekly unmasking is the show.
note: Hidden identity as a scheduled reveal rather than a permanent secret.

name: The Hologram
effect: Tupac at Coachella in 2012, which was Pepper's Ghost - the same angled glass from 1862.
note: The rhyme is the point: the modern trick is the old one with a bigger budget.

name: The Vocaloid
effect: A synthetic idol whose songs are written by thousands of fans - a performer made of the audience.
note: A card whose effect is assembled from every other card you own.

name: The Avatar
effect: Performers behind digital avatars - kayfabe reborn as a streaming industry.
note: A stamp that shows a different card entirely, and never drops it.

name: Speedrun Categories
effect: Playing games as performance - any percent, hundred percent, glitchless - and marathons for charity.
note: Endless mode with categories, which turns optimisation into its own scoreboard.

name: Twitch Plays
effect: Eighty thousand people sharing one controller - chaos as collective performance.
note: A mode where the placement is decided by vote, which is either terrible or wonderful.

name: The Flash Mob
effect: Sudden coordinated performance in public space - assembly is the trick.
note: Several token cards appear at once in a formation and vanish after one refill.

name: The Traceur
effect: Parkour and the Yamakasi - the city itself as apparatus, every wall a route.
note: Moves across the tops of stacks, ignoring what is beneath them.

name: The 900
effect: Two and a half rotations, which took eleven public failures first.
note: A card that must fail several times before it can succeed, and remembers how many.

name: Competitive Cheer
effect: Basket tosses and human pyramids under judging panels.
note: The castell mechanic, judged - the formation must be held to be scored.

name: Drone Swarm
effect: Thousands of drones replacing fireworks, drawing pictures on the night sky.
note: Props that arrange themselves into a shape above the whole board.

name: The Sphere
effect: The venue is the performance - a building-sized screen wrapping the audience.
note: The picture wall, taken to its logical end.

name: Residency Mode
effect: The tour that stops touring - the city comes to you.
note: An endless mode where one node repeats and escalates.

name: Sleep No More
effect: Masked audiences roam a hotel choosing their own show, with the famous one-on-one scenes.
note: A run where the player chooses which parts of a node to see and misses the rest.

name: The Locked Room
effect: Escape rooms - Houdini's challenge act, democratised into a global industry.
note: A timed puzzle event with the escape-artist framing already attached.

name: The ARG
effect: Games that leak out of the screen into phone booths and ciphers.
note: An out-of-game mystery, which is the deepest version of the secrets idea.

name: Meow Wolf
effect: Immersive art wandered with no fixed path - discovery as the show.
note: A node with no objective, only things to find.

name: Love is in the Bin
effect: The painting that shredded itself the moment it was auctioned, and doubled in value.
note: The Shredder card - self-destructs when sold and pays double for it.

name: Burning Man
effect: Build a city in the desert, burn the Man, and leave no trace.
note: Build-to-burn, with the empty-board bonus attached.

name: Red Bull Stratos
effect: The jump from the stratosphere, with the patron's logo on every frame of it.
note: A sponsored event - enormous reward, and the sponsor's mark on your deck afterwards.

name: Personal Bests
effect: The institution that turned feats into bookkeeping.
note: A per-card personal best, tracked across every run.

name: Competitive Eating
effect: Technique doubled the hot-dog record overnight - spectacle sport from pure method.
note: A consumption card that gets faster the more it eats.

name: The Fanchant
effect: The audience answering the stage in synchronised script - the crowd as second performer.
note: A card that scores again when the line it is in scores in a specific order.

name: The Faire
effect: Audiences who come to perform - the crowd in costume.
note: An event where audience cards join your deck as performers.

name: Scare Acting
effect: A seasonal profession built on timing, safety and the art of the near-touch.
note: A card that threatens an adjacent card without ever destroying it, and scores for the fright.

name: Found-Object Percussion
effect: Blue Man Group and Stomp - junk becomes the orchestra.
note: A card that turns every prop card in its line into a scoring instrument.

name: Handle with care
effect: Real history includes exploitation and tragedy - these ground the tone precisely because the road was hard, and must be referenced with respect rather than turned into jokes or loot.
note: The governing rule for this whole quarry. Every entry below is a specific prohibition.

name: Human exhibits
effect: Human ethnological exhibits - Ota Benga, Sarah Baartman - are never to be gamified. Full stop.
note: The only absolute prohibition in the file.

name: Animal cruelty
effect: Topsy's electrocution, Mary the elephant, fear-based training - acknowledge this by making Hagenbeck's kindness mechanically superior to consumption.
note: A constructive ruling: the humane path should also be the strong one.

name: The Hartford fire
effect: The 1944 fire's legacy of fire marshals and flameproofing works as a town rule; the unidentified victim never becomes content.
note: The Fire Marshal blind is the permitted use.

name: Performer deaths
effect: Leitzel, Codona, the Wallendas and the bullet-catch fatalities are usable as memorial framing - fragility stamps and act-retired-forever events - where the history is honoured, not punchlined.
note: Why the Aerialist leader's fragility is written as tribute rather than as a drawback.

name: Sacred performance
effect: Heyoka, Egungun, dervishes and daikagura - borrow the concepts of contrariness, stilted guardianship, spin and blessing under generic names; never borrow regalia, deity names, or claim the ritual.
note: The rule every sacred entry in this file is filed under.

name: Songlines and corroboree
effect: Knowledge systems and ceremony, not set dressing - the concept of a route remembered as a song is usable under a generic name; specific songlines, symbols and ceremony are not.
note: Why the Songlines row records the idea and refuses the mechanic.

name: Haka protocol
effect: Specific haka belong to specific iwi and carry protocol - use the generic idea of a challenge-dance opener, never reproduce ka mate or specific choreography.
note: The constraint on the haka entry.

name: Ball culture lineage
effect: Houses, categories and reading come from Black and Latino queer communities who built their own stage after exclusion from everyone else's - credit the lineage in flavour text, keep the joy, skip the caricature.
note: The constraint on the ballroom entries.

name: Romani contribution
effect: Centuries of real contribution to European music, horse arts and fairground craft - credit the virtuosity and retire the costume-shop fortune-teller cliche. The class should read as midway mitt camp, not as ethnicity.
note: The constraint that shapes the Fortune Teller class's art direction.

name: Dia de los Muertos framing
effect: Festive remembrance, not Halloween horror - the Ofrenda event should feel like a family reunion rather than a spook show.
note: The constraint on that event.

name: Kayfabe tragedies
effect: Wrestling's real history includes exploited and broken performers behind the fiction - mine the tropes, never specific people's pain.
note: The constraint on the whole kayfabe layer.

name: New spatial verbs index
effect: The game's core currency, indexed - the Courier across two columns, the Contortionist sharing a cell, the Foot Juggler's sub-slot, Walking Through the Wall, the Wing Walker's mid-flight transfer, the High Dive, the Dragon meld, the Brass Ring, the Castell crown, Keaton's one safe cell, the Crowd Surf, the Invisible Wall, the Traceur, the Clock Hang, the Puszta Five, and flooded or iced rows.
note: The single most useful page in the file for a grid game. Every one of these is a placement or movement rule nothing else in the design provides.

name: Anti-spotlight index
effect: Cards that want to be covered - the Mango Seed, Cyr's Backlift, the Turk, the Spirit Cabinet, X-Ray Eyes, Humbug, the Incubator, the costaleros who add their rank to their carrier, and the water-puppet operators.
note: Height stacking made this whole family playable, and it is the counterweight the spotlight system needs.

name: Deck-position index
effect: Extending Heavy, Light and the Act types - the Ambitious Card, the Marked stamp, the Bottom Deal, the Hunger Artist and the Holdout.
note: Five cards that all manipulate one number nothing else touches.

name: Economy index
effect: Canfield's house rules, money-suited cards, Ticket Stubs, the Forged Ace, Snake Oil, the Rat Sheet, brass checks, the Dubplate, the claque racket, Sponsorship, the Shredder and the Hat.
note: Twelve economy hooks, none of which needs a second currency to work.

name: The duel system
effect: One alternating one-upmanship minigame with twelve regional skins - flyting, repentistas and payadores, extempo, balagtasan, the scissors dance, cutting contests, reading, katajjaq, jugalbandi, lip sync, Sharman's boxing tent and Greenlandic drum duels.
note: Build it once and skin it globally. The best return on effort anywhere in the compendium.

name: The ban-workaround family
effect: Towns ban and cards adapt - capoeira, steelpan, the gumboot code, hanafuda, Czech puppets, frevo umbrellas and wrestling's blind spot. Oppression into invention is the most repeated story in world performance.
note: A core mechanic loop rather than a card family, and the most thematically loaded thing in the file.

name: The protection family
effect: One bodyguard verb with many faces - the rodeo clown, the target girl, the stunt double, the mime escort, the Vine stamp and Lloyd's Policy.
note: Six cards, one mechanic, and the counterplay layer every hazard blind needs.

name: Build-to-burn
effect: Investment cards that pay out on destruction - Las Fallas with its pardoned ninot, and Burning Man with Leave No Trace as an empty-board bonus.
note: The only card family whose reward requires you to lose the board.

name: Boss and town batch two
effect: Hall of Mirrors, the Marathon, Exposition City, jaded cities, the Riot of the Factions, the Faro Bank, the day-and-date Showdown, the Balance boss, the Prepared Town, the Gong, the Scam Booking, the two-faction city and the Loggione.
note: Thirteen blinds already named here, and every one of them is in the blinds file.

name: The kayfabe layer
effect: Wrestling's gift taken wholesale - the Kayfabe rule card under which Gaffs count as real, face and heel alignment, Heat as a second currency, the Belt stamp, the Mask Wager, the Streak, the Screwjob once per profile, and the designated loser's one-in-a-thousand win.
note: A complete subsystem, already coherent, and carnival-descended so it fits the theme exactly.

name: Secrets batch two
effect: The four-by-thirteen Voladores calendar, the yakuza hand, the Dead Man's Hand, the Disaster March audio tell, Zip's unanswered question, the named court cards, the uncredited artist, Buchinger's micro-text, the rope trick that becomes real, the Scottish Play ritual, the rider's hidden clause, wax-and-gold double text, the out-of-game mystery, and duende as unpurchasable transcendence.
note: Fourteen secrets, none of which needs an answer to work.

name: Meta structures index
effect: The Academy, the dynasties, the Kellar to Thurston succession, the social-circus school, Winter Quarters, Residency mode, speedrun-category endless modes, the seasonal crown, per-card personal bests, and the busker-to-space arc.
note: Ten meta-progression shapes, each with a real institution behind it.

name: Naming gifts
effect: Call the acts The Pledge, The Turn and The Prestige; call the final city The Palace; call the discard Showmen's Rest.
note: Three free names. The first is now historical - the three acts are gone - but The Palace and Showmen's Rest still stand.

name: The five stories
effect: The stories worth full flavour-text treatment - Couney's incubators, Blackstone's calm evacuation, Adelaide Herrmann's bullet catch, Reginald Scot's merciful expose, Pablo Fanque's poster becoming a Beatles song, Marceau's silent children, the steelpan's invention, the Generals' 1971 win, the enxaneta's raised hand, and Love is in the Bin.
note: Ten true stories, each of which makes a card memorable without a single invented word.

name: Reference table separators
effect: The column separators of the four reference tables that open Parts C, D, E and G.
note: Markdown structure, recorded so every line of the compendium is accounted for.

name: The organized record
effect: The design document is the draft compiled into topics, cross-referenced against the code, preserving each topic's history as a mini-timeline that always ends with the latest state. Nothing is deleted, including abandoned ideas.
note: The one doc that says what the owner decided rather than what an agent proposed. Its status legend - implemented, partial, designed, sketch, abandoned, summary-only - is what makes it auditable.

name: Identity and pitch
effect: Solatro - Balatro, but the hand-play is solitaire. A circus deckbuilder where the Ringmaster arranges performers in the Ring to excite the audience, touring a generated world.
note: The pitch survived the overhaul word for word; only the shape of the Ring changed.

name: Stated references
effect: Balatro, the Zachtronics collection, Hempuli, Deadman Wonderland, FTL, Slay the Spire, TFT, One Step From Eden, Umamusume, Vampire Survivors, Mewgenics, Inscryption, Steel Ball Run and Titanium Court.
note: Each reference is attached to the system it informed, which is what makes the list usable rather than decorative.

name: Design philosophy one-liners
effect: Scoring contextualises every card; a run should yak-shave the player into a new plan; flexibility is part of a card's budget; do not multiply progression systems; secrets drive engagement without answers.
note: Five rulings that between them decide most balance arguments before they start.

name: Loop v1
effect: Deck-click drops with score slots on the right, mulliganable and rearrangeable incoming cards.
note: Superseded twice - first by whole-board submit, then by the grid.

name: Loop v2
effect: Whole-board submit - draw continuously, press Submit to evaluate the entire board, which then clears and reseeds from the Entrance.
note: Superseded by the grid. Scoring now fires on completion and End clears nothing.

name: Undo is always live
effect: Undo during a resolving act cancels it with nothing committed, and undo at the outcome screen rewinds the final Submit. Fame banks at Continue rather than at the outcome screen, so a win stays undoable until committed.
note: Shipped, and the banking rule is the subtle part - it is what stops a resumed win double-banking.

name: Loop implementation state
effect: The game class with its draw deck, discard, Entrance and Ring, where the Entrance card drops stacks and refills from the deck, and one rule card performs the evaluation.
note: Every part survived the overhaul except the drop - the Entrance now hands cards over rather than dropping them.

name: Board and zones
effect: Five columns chosen so a full row is a poker hand; two zones renamed Grand Entrance and the Ring; the column count set by rule cards rather than hardcoded; duplicate rule cards identified by rank; null cards; expanding zone controls; the board as an array.
note: The five-wide choice is the one decision the whole overhaul rests on. The immutability worry resolved itself - zones exist, but the count is five separate cards.

name: Stacking and movement
effect: Illegal stacks could once only go to the submission spot; then only legal stacks could be lifted at all; the legal stack is an ascending or descending run of differing suits, decided by a resolver that gathers allow and deny votes.
note: The resolver survived the overhaul untouched, which is why stacking upward needed no new rules.

name: Scoring timeline
effect: Cribbage counting, then dual-axis rows and columns with the two totals multiplied, then the combo reframe where the payout is the row total times the column total times the combo.
note: The three-bucket product is the fourth entry in this timeline, and the first one that had to account for diagonals.

name: Performance rings
effect: Score zones by board depth - the first five rows at one multiple, the next band at two, and so on outward.
note: Now a height band rather than a row band, because the board grows upward.

name: Trigger order
effect: Field effects, then the deck top-down, then the board left to right and top to bottom including the Entrance, then the discard newest first.
note: Unchanged except that the board walk now covers every grid in turn.

name: Big numbers
effect: Planned from the start with an infinite number class, and never a single digit.
note: Shipped. The grid's score buckets are the newest thing that had to learn to pack them.

name: Avalanche filed
effect: After scoring, every card on the board attacks the scoreboard, reducing the goal by the number of cards.
note: The prototype for every goal-manipulating effect, and still the only one.

name: Card anatomy
effect: Suit, rank, stamp slot, skill slot and type; one parent and one child; a board of zones plus three decks; the layout parsed from the rules at creation; the scoring UI deliberately not card-implemented.
note: The engine contract, all of it implemented, and none of it changed by the overhaul.

name: Vocabulary timeline
effect: Seals became Stamps; card materials became Types; the stamp might yet become a diegetic hat or a piece of costume.
note: The newest draft weighed a second equipment slot and judged it overkill.

name: Pip architecture
effect: One comparator for every pip interaction with mods polled before any numeric fallback; each pip owning its visuals; pips able to register their own scoring methods; pip effects permanently active; the wild pip tracking what it copies.
note: Implemented as designed, which is unusual enough to be worth noting.

name: Determinism
effect: Everything deterministic, with a hand-written generator the engine cannot change and per-seed random offsets rather than one shared seed.
note: The map side is fully seeded already; the game side is not.

name: Spotlight timeline
effect: From all revealed cards act, to abilities needing to be visible with a stamp exempting them, to the Spotlight rebrand where an unblocked card is in the spotlight.
note: Implemented. Height stacking is what finally made covering a decision rather than an accident.

name: Spotlight presentation
effect: Cards peeking over their blockers, literal spotlight beams instead of glow, the eye stamp showing a miniature of its skill art, the show-all-actives toggle and the compress-board view.
note: The reveal offset shipped as part of the grid layout; the two buttons are still wanted.

name: The rule deck
effect: A hidden deck of cards defining the defaults, which the player can modify during a run; boss effects as temporary cards that destroy themselves; vouchers in the main deck; Baba-is-you visibility rules; rule cards carrying random pips; the rule deck resolving last; input slots as cards; game laws as plain text; true vision as a prestige unlock; a rules-in-hand deck variant; per-scenario rule decks; the level-deck idea rejected; a force-trigger card; a rulesets pack; and the vetoed playable-deck idea.
note: The single most productive idea in the document. The blinds category is its newest dividend.

name: Circus vocabulary table
effect: Grand Entrance and the Ring, performers and feats, prop cards, exciting the audience, the Ringmaster, conventions, spotlight, cue, talent packs, the presentation stage, the carnival, the traveling troupe, and shows at towns.
note: Overscore and tips are marked retired in the table, which the newest economy work may reverse.

name: Suits and projectiles
effect: Four standard suits today and a circus roster planned; scored cards spawning props of their suit by rank; knives and hoops travelling the row, balls and flames the column; then the balance pass giving knives the plain cards and hoops the talents.
note: Shipped in full, including the balance pass.

name: Suit-props contract
effect: Nominal suit subclasses with no ordering, factory switching with a random roster, firing once per meld membership, the knife kept as the hoop's mirror, fire as a count buff through the Burning status, the mancala walk for ballistic targeting, props as transient composed modifiers, no randomness inside the simulation, and a view layer that only interpolates.
note: The tightest contract in the codebase, and the reason a fifth suit would be one file.

name: Leaders and classes
effect: Leaders start on the board or in the Entrance and survive scoring; the Ringmaster is the example spec; eleven classes each with a mechanical identity; groups that leaders boost; and the three Act types controlling deck position.
note: The class list is the taxonomy every card in the catalog is filed under.

name: Cues and charges
effect: Right-click to cue with a glowing halo divided by remaining charges; one shared charge system; effects that latch on permanently; buttons built as cards; and an info toggle for full descriptions.
note: The halo's divided-not-resized design is the good detail here.

name: Special decks
effect: The magic deck of elements, the survivor deck of supplies, Double Everything, rules-in-hand, the custom deck as the final unlock, and deck unlocks doubling as gimmick runs.
note: Double Everything is the deck the grid allotment rule most rewards.

name: The catalog
effect: The card spreadsheet - skills, stamps, types, rule cards, and the summary-only cards that an auto-summary invented rather than the owner.
note: The catalog is now the file this rewrite gave axis columns to.

name: Catalog skills
effect: Extra Point, Echoing Trigger, Hungry Hippo, Sin of Gluttony, Frankenstein, Sliced Bread, Gold, Exchange Voucher, the three God cards, Mystery Box, Pandora's Box, Utter Chaos, HONK, Avalanche, Storyteller, Presentation, Cheat Day, Press Bribery, the rarity chain, Spiderweb, Poker Crown, Column Poker, Genie's Wish, the discard joker, the charge acrobat, the reroll blessing, the Ringmaster and the Label rule card.
note: Twenty-eight cards, of which six are implemented and the rest are restated for the grid in this file.

name: Catalog stamps
effect: Double Trigger, Revealing, Global, Money on Trigger, Maximum Effort and the always-grabbable stamp.
note: Three shipped, three still designed.

name: Catalog types
effect: Paper, Stone, Heavy, Light, the four elementals, Input, Booster, the three Acts, Leader and Immovable.
note: Water's elemental behaviour is the one entry the grid superseded outright.

name: Catalog rule cards
effect: The input adders, the zone adders, the OG grabber and placer, the cascade scorer, the poker evaluator, boss rules and swappable ruleset defaults.
note: The cascade scorer and the zone adder are the two the grid replaced; everything else carried over.

name: Summary-only cards
effect: Cards an auto-summary invented rather than the owner - Helium, The Acrobat, The Anarchist, Ghost Card, Searing Knife, Sliced Reality, the Tappable Clown, the Wildcard Pip, and Symmetrical Show, which turned out to be genuinely user-authored.
note: Flagging provenance like this is what let the recommendations adopt three and reject two on the record.

name: Map timeline
effect: The minesweeper board, then the triangle map that was actually built, then biome-world sketches, then the FTL constellation world tour.
note: Only the last one survives, and the worldgen addon already renders it.

name: Map content and UX
effect: Packs or rarer singles at nodes, a preview with a separate confirm, biome unlocks with the Mewgenics caution attached, pre-generated maps on a background thread, procedural biome fill and the star-wars scroll for card choice.
note: The Mewgenics caution is the owner flagging their own idea as a risk, which is worth preserving.

name: Economy
effect: Cards are the currency with no abstract gold; the shop prices in stacks of your own cards; mana cards as an alternative; shops built from the board; the carnival as the meta shop; and an exponential power curve because flexibility is part of a budget.
note: The pricing philosophy is the one line the catalog's cost column should be audited against.

name: Turn resources
effect: The discard essay, one free undo per turn baked in, an extra reroll per game, and cards that cannot be retired until they have scored or triggered.
note: The discard essay is now the strongest argument for what the Entrance refill should cost.

name: Rarity and packs
effect: The card spreadsheet plan, rarity borders and shines, power-sorted rarity chains, arena-style pack mulligans, slot-machine pack opening and secret melds added by cards as they enter the deck.
note: Power-sorted rarity is the only definition of rarity here that can be checked mechanically.

name: Meta progression
effect: Card unlocks on a shared pass, prestige spent at the carnival, deck unlocks merged with gimmick runs, ascensions with their prestige overlap flagged, community and lore treated sceptically, event-recycled prestige, a retire button, and persistence hooks carrying score between shows.
note: The ascension-prestige overlap warning is the owner catching their own system multiplication.

name: The optimization essay
effect: Deckbuilders chasing one number collapse into hyperfocus; formation-based win conditions do not scale; and the answer is boss blinds - negative effects that test whether a deck can handle anything.
note: The essay that produced the blinds category, and the reason every blind targets a different pillar.

name: Difficulty levers
effect: The goal increment per match, the fame wager, progress gates behind extreme scores, quests, and Mewgenics-style debuffs like Exhausted.
note: The goal curve's refit is still open as its own phase.

name: Events and encounters
effect: The genie's wish, history-driven events like the union strike and the taxman, minigame events with puzzle win conditions, the forbidden-solitaire variant and temporary prestige.
note: History-driven events are the cheapest way to make a run feel like it happened.

name: Art direction
effect: From 3D-ish hovering motion to the stylized static look, with the budget moved into sound.
note: The direction the card flip followed.

name: Visual ideas
effect: The starfield, card art as background, the end-of-round swirl into the score numerals, the tornado into the deck, cards rising while scoring, screen shake with a camera shift, goofy travel animations, crunchy sound and cursor attraction, the slot-machine pack, rarity shines and the star-wars scroll.
note: The swirl and the tornado both belong to End now, which is the only moment the board empties.

name: The appended summary
effect: The auto-summary added little to the vision and architecture sections, invented several cards, and contributed a genuinely useful seed-systems appendix - independent RNG streams per subsystem, predetermined queues for shareable seeds, roll-then-discard for profile-stable seeds, and anti-repeat weight decay.
note: Four concrete seeding rules that the determinism work should implement verbatim.

name: The vetoed registry
effect: Cribbage scoring, the deck-click loop, the submission spot, the minesweeper map, the triangle map that was built, map-card seeding, playable decks, custom rule decks, the level deck, scoring-as-cards, formation win conditions, node parenting, 3D hover motion, fifteens as default, and the mana bar - each with the reason it was dropped.
note: Fifteen dead ends with their reasons preserved, which is what stops them being reinvented. Several are now revivable under the grid.

name: The reality check
effect: The prototype TODO list tracked against the code, item by item, and an explicit list of where the dream and the build disagree.
note: The habit worth keeping - a doc that states its own gap with the code.

name: Where they disagree
effect: The spotlight shipped, the rule-deck architecture shipped, deterministic RNG streams did not, and the pack mulligan, shop, economy, meta progression, leaders, acts and circus vocabulary are all still design rather than code.
note: The honest list of what remains, and mostly unchanged by the overhaul - which was about the board, not the run.

name: Map implementation state
effect: The worldgen addon bakes a seeded heightmap world into a node graph with ferry edges and threaded loading; the game side drives token traversal, assigns node roles deterministically from the seed, launches shows with fame requirements from the goal curve, forces five-card packs at booster nodes, persists runs, and reverses the tour end to start for endless mode with goals scaling per lap.
note: Shipped. Still unbuilt - tips, fog of war, the hype wager and tour planning. The addon is vendored, so never edit the copy inside the game project.
